entries.name: Modern Running Sheet

rows: Pay off the Iron Covenant ledger and reveal that the criminal network is centralized enough for someone else to use it.
Infiltrate or assault Koven House, seize Covenant ledgers, free prisoners, break the local command structure.
Stakeout, secret entry, captured courier, roof approach, service tunnels, negotiation, or direct assault.

The Koven House lead has already paid off; the question here is how much evidence and how many witnesses survive. At least one ledger cache, the prisoner testimony, and the command cache provide redundant proof.
Mission 2 of 5. All four PCs are paid 75 gp each on completion.
The Iron Covenant deliberately unified multiple gangs, but some orders are now appearing without any Covenant officer claiming responsibility.

entries: {@i Use the existing Koven House map, concealed routes, roof access, courtyard, and service corridors.}
{@b Finite whole-site roster:} 1 {@creature Bandit Captain|XMM} Covenant Factor, 4 Spies, 4 Thugs, and 2 Scouts. No room creates extra defenders.
{@b Outer Yard:} 1 Scout + 1 Thug.
{@b Auxiliary Buildings:} 1 Spy + 1 Scout.
{@b Service Corridors:} 1 Spy + 1 Thug.
{@b Command Room:} Covenant Factor + 2 Spies + 2 Thugs.
{@b Morale:} ordinary defenders flee or surrender when their route out is cut off, the Factor falls, or the ledgers are already lost.

entries.name: Rewards and Treasure
entries: Council pay: {@b 75 gp per PC}, including Pepper.
Recovered portable criminal wealth totals about {@b 1,500 gp}, but most of it is identifiable stolen property. Returning it creates witnesses and goodwill rather than becoming automatic party loot.
The Council releases one unclaimed {@item Shield +1|XDMG} from the seized armory to the party after the evidence is logged.
Consumables: 1 {@item Potion of Greater Healing|XDMG} and 1 {@item Potion of Invisibility|XDMG}.

entries.name: The Iron Covenant at Koven House
entries: Koven House is {@b an Iron Covenant headquarters}.
The Covenant is not a dragon cult and does not worship Tyren. Its leadership believes it has built a profitable criminal coalition with political protection and unusually reliable financing.

Perrin’s original purpose was political. Through intermediaries, he encouraged the Covenant to bring competing gangs into one structure. Increased organized crime would make the Council look incapable. When the city became frightened enough, Perrin intended to support the crackdown, destroy the network, and step forward as the person who restored order.
Tyren saw a different opportunity: Perrin had gathered a large number of compromised, connected people into one communication system.
Koven House is where Tyren begins treating that system like a nervous system.

entries.name: Getting the Job
entries: The Kellan documents and the coded Blackstone ledger point toward the same place after Council clerks compare routing shorthand.

Lessa Dorn and Kav Orin can assist by placing old property boundaries over the recovered delivery routes. Their work establishes that multiple routes terminate at the same mansion compound: Koven House.
Ulric authorizes a warrant once the documentary connection is strong enough.
Wern wants the party to move before the Covenant burns records.
Perrin agrees that immediate action is justified. This is not an act. He genuinely wants this Covenant node broken now that he knows the Spirit is issuing instructions through it without him.

entries.name: Table-Ready Opposition
entries: Use the finite roster above. Defenders know the house, use doors and concealed routes, and prioritize records and escape over dying in place.
Defenders from a bypassed area stay where they are until an alarm or clear reason makes them move. They do not teleport into later encounters.

On an alarm, the two nearest non-command defenders move toward the disturbance while the remaining outer defenders secure exits. The command-room force stays with the Factor and the evidence unless the party forces a different response.

entries.name: Interactive Traps
entries: Preserve the old house’s prepared-defense identity, but every hazard needs a tell and a countermeasure.

rows: old horizontal cut marks; new tension wire
DC 14 Perception notices. DC 14 Dexterity with thieves’ tools disables. Trigger: DC 14 Dex save, 3d6 slashing, half on success.
DC 14 Perception. Trigger: DC 14 Con save, 2d6 poison and Blinded until end of next turn; half and no blindness on success.
Characters can shore it up or move carefully. Trigger: DC 14 Dex save, 3d6 bludgeoning, half on success; rubble becomes Difficult Terrain.
Initiative starts when sealed. Three rounds to escape, block nozzles, or prevent ignition. Burning creatures take 2d6 fire at end of turn until out or fire suppressed.
DC 14 Dex save or Restrained. Action and DC 12 Strength check, or cutting the net, frees a target.
DC 14 Dex save or fall 10 feet, 1d6 bludgeoning, Prone.

entries: A trap that sounds an alarm advances the house response instead of simply adding more damage.

entries.name: 1. Outer Yard
entries: The mansion exterior looks better maintained than surrounding ruins. Someone has money, workers, and reasons to preserve it.
Characters watching for an hour see couriers arrive separately and leave by different routes. The couriers wear no common uniform.
One detail is shared: every courier touches a black iron-nail cross fixed beneath the gate lintel before being admitted.
{@b Deployment.} 1 Scout watches the gate/roofline while 1 Thug controls access. If bypassed quietly, they remain outside.

{@b Observation.} Ten minutes of watching reveals courier timing automatically. A {@dc 13} Insight, Investigation, or Perception check after one minute reveals that couriers use separate routes but the same admission ritual.

entries.name: 2. Auxiliary Buildings
entries: Use these for surveillance, a hidden service entrance, or a neutral creature/squatter that has learned to avoid the Covenant.

If using the existing quickling encounter seed, keep the quickling {@b unnamed and nonrecurring}. Respectful characters can learn that people inside sometimes walk through the house at night “like they’re dreaming.”
{@b Deployment.} 1 Spy and 1 Scout use the auxiliary structures as a listening post and fallback point. They avoid a stand-up fight if they can warn the house or escape.

entries.name: 3. Service Corridors
entries: The Iron Covenant uses concealed corridors to move between rooms, attack from advantage, and retreat.
A character who captures a map, spends ten minutes searching a known section, or follows a withdrawing defender can discover a route without needing a single pass/fail roll.
The first important cache contains duplicates of Kellan’s shift schedules and the same color coding.
{@b Deployment.} 1 Spy and 1 Thug patrol the service routes. If surprised or cut off, they retreat toward the nearest exit rather than the command room.

A character who searches a known wall or follows a withdrawing defender finds the concealed route automatically. A {@dc 14} Investigation check finds one quickly when the party only knows that a concealed route exists.

entries.name: 4. Prison and Blackmail Rooms
entries: The Covenant keeps debtors, informants, and blackmail targets here. Most prisoners know only ordinary criminal information.

One prisoner reports something useful: the Covenant Factor recently punished a lieutenant for issuing an order the Factor swore he never gave. Three witnesses heard the Factor’s voice give the instruction.
The Factor blamed impersonation.
This is the first evidence that the impossible coordination may involve more than couriers and paperwork.
There are {@b four prisoners}: two debtors, one blackmail target, and one former Covenant courier. None are combatants.
If freed and given a reasonable chance to leave safely, the former courier provides the unauthorized-order testimony without a check. Social checks only affect willingness to testify publicly later.

entries.name: 5. Ledger Room
entries: The ledgers establish the Covenant’s structure.
The essential discoveries are automatic once the room is secured:

items: competing gangs were paid bonuses for operating under shared schedules;
the Covenant financed neutral meeting sites and compensated gangs for settling old feuds;
money entered the network through ordinary-looking commercial channels;
one channel leads to a Cardon-connected intermediary, but the paper trail stops before proving Perrin ordered crimes;
several payments were authorized using a code {@b not found anywhere in the Covenant’s own key}.

entries: That unknown code appears only on instructions that produced no obvious profit: moving people to particular buildings, changing patrol routes, gathering crowds, or keeping specific streets busy at specific times.
These are Tyren’s experiments.
{@b Evidence redundancy.} If this room is burned or stripped, a duplicate payment ledger remains in the Command Cache and the former courier can still establish the unauthorized-order problem.

entries.name: 6. Covenant Factor
entries: The command-room force is exactly the Covenant Factor, 2 Spies, and 2 Thugs.
The Factor begins beside the main ledger case. One Spy is responsible for moving the command cache; the other covers the escape route. The Thugs hold the doorway or nearest choke point.
The Factor uses a {@creature Bandit Captain|XMM} stat block and has 2 {@b Spies} nearby if the party reaches the command room before breaking the house response.

entries.name: Portraying the Factor
entries: The Factor looks more like a prosperous fixer than a street criminal: good coat, clean hands, expensive pen, and a small visible piece of Iron Covenant ironwork worn as if it were a business credential. The Factor speaks softly and assumes everyone has a price, a fear, or a practical reason to compromise.

This NPC should feel dangerous because of {@b competence and information}, not because of theatrical cruelty. The Factor knows names, debts, schedules, who can be leaned on, and which local disputes can be turned into leverage. The unnerving crack in that confidence is the command problem inside the Covenant: orders have been given in familiar voices without the supposed speakers remembering them.

When pressed on those incidents, the Factor becomes defensive in a very specific way—less "that is impossible" and more "someone has compromised my system." The Factor still believes there is a human explanation.
The Factor knows the following:

items: an outside patron paid the Covenant to unify criminal operations;
the patron never appeared personally;
the arrangement was supposed to be profitable and politically protected;
somebody has recently begun issuing orders through the network without paying and without using recognized Covenant authority;
people who receive those orders often insist afterward that they made the choice themselves.

entries: The Factor assumes a rival has compromised the organization.
If captured alive, the Factor can identify the commercial intermediary but cannot identify Perrin.

entries.name: Alarm, Rest, and Withdrawal
entries: The party can take a Short Rest inside Koven House, but the organization continues moving during the hour.
If the house is not yet alerted, missed rotations and absent lookouts eventually expose the intrusion. By the end of the rest, the Factor has the command room prepared and portable evidence packed.

If the house is already alerted, the Factor moves the duplicate ledger into the Command Cache, orders obvious incriminating papers burned, and sends any bypassed outer defenders to secure exits rather than pile into one room.
A Short Rest therefore restores the party but increases defender preparation and reduces the amount of easy evidence.

If the party withdraws entirely, the Covenant begins evacuating the headquarters. Returning later is still possible, but the Factor may be gone and the party will rely more heavily on the fixed ledgers, prisoners, and property records.

entries.name: 7. Command Cache
entries: A hidden command cache contains the best evidence and one disturbing object: a page where several different hands have copied the same sentence in nearly identical wording.
{@b We know where we are needed. We will be there.}
None of the writers remember being told to write it.
Present this as contradictory testimony and impossible command behavior; the player-facing description does not identify it as mind control.

The cache is fire-resistant and deliberately separate from the Ledger Room. Even if the main ledgers are destroyed, it preserves one payment ledger, the unknown authorization code, and enough routing information to prove centralized Covenant coordination.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The house contains about {@b 1,500 gp} in portable criminal wealth, most of it identifiable as stolen property.
Council pay is {@b 75 gp per PC}.
The party receives one {@item Shield +1|XDMG}, 1 {@item Potion of Greater Healing|XDMG}, and 1 {@item Potion of Invisibility|XDMG} after the seizure is documented.

entries.name: Resting, Alarm, and Time
entries: The party can attempt a Short Rest inside Koven House, but the house continues operating during that hour.
If the Factor is not yet alerted, missed rotations reveal the intrusion before the rest ends. The command room becomes fully prepared and the best ledger copy is moved to the command cache.

If the Factor is already alerted, one hour is enough to burn one secondary ledger cache and begin evacuating through the service route. The essential Koven/Perrin intermediary trail still survives in the command cache or prisoner testimony.

If the party leaves the property entirely for roughly two hours, the Factor evacuates surviving personnel and the portable 600 gp Covenant reserve. The 900 gp identifiable property and at least one essential ledger remain because moving everything quickly is impossible.

entries.name: Fail-Forward and Site Aftermath

rows: The party still gets the ledgers and intermediary trail; the Factor becomes a possible later witness or fugitive, not a required recurring villain.
Ledgers, prisoners, and payment records provide the same campaign lead.
The command cache contains a duplicate routing ledger with the essential evidence.
The same impossible-order incident appears in a Factor memorandum.
The Council can still seize the house once the command structure is broken.

entries: After the operation, Council clerks and victim representatives inventory the site. Koven House stops functioning as the Covenant's Bellweather headquarters. Surviving Covenant cells become decentralized rather than disappearing from the world.

entries.name: Resolution
entries: Koven House is operationally broken when the Factor can no longer coordinate the site and the party secures at least one surviving evidence source.

Within hours, Wern seals the main entrances and posts a small Council detail while clerks inventory property and victims identify stolen goods. Surviving Covenant members disperse rather than immediately forming a replacement headquarters.
Koven House is broken when the Factor is captured, killed, driven out, or loses the ability to coordinate the Covenant cell and the party secures the ledgers.

The Iron Covenant survives as an organization unless the party takes extraordinary steps. What breaks here is its central Bellweather headquarters and the political usefulness of this particular network.

entries.name: DM Truth: Perrin’s Second Off-Ramp
entries: Perrin now has documentary confirmation that the Spirit is issuing commands through the organization he created.
He also sees a benefit.

The Covenant becomes easier to destroy because frightened criminals are behaving predictably. Perrin can publicly support the raid and privately tell himself that the Spirit merely helped clean up the mess Perrin intended to clean up eventually.
He does not confess.
His rationalization changes from {@b “I didn’t authorize that”} to {@b “the result was still useful.”}

entries.name: Pepper: Mission 2 Complete
entries: If Pepper completes the authorized mission and returns to Ledger House, mark {@b Mission 2 of 5 complete}. She is paid normally from this point forward.
Lessa and Kav may verify the recovered property routes or assist the Council in documenting the house. They do not become investigators of Caleb’s death; that matter is already known and adjudicated.
Mission pay is {@b 75 gp for each of the four PCs}.

entries.name: Milestone
entries: Advance the party to {@b level 5} after Koven House is broken.

entries.name: Modern Running Sheet

rows: Transform the current criminal mystery into a historical mystery: Bellweather has seen impossible coordination before.
Reach the keep, survive or bypass bound defenders, recover the final garrison records, stop hostile agents from destroying them.
Research passwords, use the old oath, parley with spirits, force entry, or exploit conflict between old defenders and current raiders.
The historical truth exists in the diary, chapel witness, command-stone report, and civic circular. Losing one source reduces context; it cannot erase the Tyren/Unturned discovery.
Mission 3 of 5. All four PCs receive 75 gp each.
Old Bellweather’s defenders recorded the same one-mind behavior fifty years ago and referred to a few resistant people as the Unturned.
