{@b Finite old-defender roster:} 4 Skeletons, 4 Zombies, 2 Specters, and 1 Wight.
{@b Shore and Gate:} 2 Skeletons + 2 Zombies.
{@b Courtyard:} 2 Zombies + 1 Specter.
{@b Barracks Archive:} 2 Skeletons.
{@b Old Chapel:} 1 Specter, which can become a witness instead of a combatant.
{@b Command Stone:} 1 Wight, the last command element.
{@b Record-burning strike team:} 1 Veteran, 2 Bugbears, 2 Guards, and 2 Scouts. This team is separate from the old defenders and does not gain extra members.

entries.name: Rewards and Treasure
entries: Council pay: {@b 75 gp per PC}.
Recovered salvage and ceremonial equipment worth {@b 500 gp}.
Magic rewards: 1 {@item Potion of Heroism|XDMG} and 1 {@item Shield +1|XDMG}.

rows: 1 Specter, usually social if approached respectfully

entries.name: Why Savin Keep Matters Now
entries: The Koven ledgers contain routing references to old harbor records and a pre-fall military code. Ulric’s clerks identify Savin Keep as the last place that code was formally used.
The Council is not sending the party to “reclaim the next district.” It wants the records before the Iron Covenant or another interested party destroys them.
Wern is particularly interested because the same coordination pattern could represent a military threat.
Brann is interested because descriptions of memory loss and involuntary behavior resemble possession or enchantment.
Perrin wants the records recovered too. He is now quietly desperate to understand what the Spirit really is, though he does not tell the party that.

entries.name: The Old Defender Oath
entries: Preserve the existing challenge-and-response/password structure. The fragments {@b Lux}, {@b Shestnik}, and {@b Samosud} remain useful old garrison terms.
Characters can find enough fragments through records, plaques, and the approach to bypass some undead guardians. The passwords are advantages, not gates that can stall the adventure.
Treat the three surviving fragments—{@b Lux}, {@b Shestnik}, and {@b Samosud}—as cumulative proof of authority rather than pass/fail passwords.

With one authentic fragment, old defenders hesitate and allow a brief parley before attacking. With two fragments, the party can bypass one old-defender group without combat. With all three, the Wight recognizes the party as acting under Bellweather authority and allows access to the Command Stone unless the party attacks first.

A character studying an oath plaque or surviving garrison document can recover a missing fragment with ten minutes of careful examination. A {@dc 13} History, Religion, or Investigation check finds it in one minute instead.

entries.name: 1. Shore and Gate
entries: Old remains near the landing include a corroded medallion and part of a watch schedule.
Recent tracks show that another small team arrived within the last two days. Their objective is not occupation; they are looking for records.
The undead defenders respond to the old password or to clear evidence that the visitors are acting under Bellweather authority.
Use {@b Skeletons}, {@b Zombies}, {@b Specters}, and one {@creature Wight|XMM} across the chapter rather than a mass battle.
{@b Deployment.} 2 Skeletons and 2 Zombies hold the landing. They do not pursue far from the gate unless the command structure remains hostile.

entries.name: 2. Courtyard
entries: The bound defenders still follow the final orders they received fifty years ago.
If combat occurs, one spirit repeatedly says:
{@b “Hold until the Unturned reach the lower chamber.”}
This is the first use of the historical term. The term appears here without explanation.
{@b Deployment.} 2 Zombies and 1 Specter patrol the courtyard. They react to the oath procedure before initiative begins.

entries.name: 3. Barracks Archive
entries: A hidden diary from the final week before Bellweather fell describes soldiers receiving contradictory orders.
Useful fragments:
{@b “By the seventh day, even the watch answered with one voice. Orders passed without messenger or horn.”}
{@b “We changed the countersign twice. It did not matter. Men who had not attended the briefing knew it before sunset.”}
{@b “Three in the east barracks still hear the pressure and remain themselves. Chaplain calls them Unturned.”}
The diary never says dragon.
{@b Deployment.} 2 Skeletons guard the archive entrance. The diary is recovered automatically once the room is secured or the defenders recognize authority.

entries.name: 4. Old Chapel
entries: The final chaplain’s spirit can be used if the party approaches respectfully. The spirit is a one-scene witness rather than an ongoing NPC.
The spirit remembers fragments, not a lecture.
It can establish:

items: the enemy was called {@b Tyren} in sealed military reports;
Tyren could “speak through” citizens and soldiers;
a few people could resist;
those people went beneath Varen Keep with civic mages and priests;
after that night, the voices stopped;
the survivors refused to record the full ritual in one place.

entries: The spirit points toward {@b Marren Library} as the repository that received copies of pre-fall magical research.

{@b Deployment.} 1 Specter manifests here. Respectful invocation of the old oath, Bellweather authority, or burial rites turns the scene into conversation; otherwise the Specter defends the chapel until bloodied, then tries to communicate.

entries.name: 5. Command Stone
entries: The binding focus for the undead defenders remains active.

Speaking the release phrase found in the chapel ends the ordinary defenders’ duty and allows them to rest. If the party instead destroys the focus, the same result occurs but damages one archive room.
A sealed report beneath the stone contains the campaign’s first explicit Tyren line:
{@b TYREN — CONTROL EVENT. Civilian spread accelerating. Standard command compromised. Use Unturned personnel for all communication regarding Varen.}
No creature type is listed.
{@b Deployment.} 1 Wight acts as the last command element. If the party has all three oath fragments, it stands down and witnesses the release of the defenders.

entries.name: 6. Record-Burning Strike Team
entries: The strike team arrives once the party has opened the Command Stone area or after roughly one hour of obvious activity in the keep.
Use exactly 1 Veteran, 2 Bugbears, and 4 Guards. The Veteran and Bugbears hold the approach. Two Guards carry oil and torches toward the archive. Two Guards cover the withdrawal route.

{@b Burning records.} There are three vulnerable record bundles in the archive. A burner adjacent to a bundle can ignite it with an action. A burning bundle is lost at the end of the next round unless a character uses an action with water, a blanket, suitable magic, or another obviously effective method. An improvised uncertain method uses a {@dc 13} appropriate check.

The essential Tyren/Unturned story has redundancy: the sealed report beneath the Command Stone survives even if all three vulnerable bundles burn. Saving more bundles preserves context, names, and corroboration.
The strike team withdraws if the Veteran falls, both Bugbears fall, or the archive objective is clearly lost. They are paid professionals, not fanatics.
{@b Trigger.} The strike team reaches the keep when the party secures the Command Stone or spends about twenty minutes inside the archive complex, whichever happens first.
{@b Starting roles.} The Veteran and 2 Bugbears screen the party. The 2 Scouts take covered firing positions. The 2 Guards carry oil and tinder to the archive.

{@b Burning records.} The archive has three document zones. A Guard adjacent to an unburned zone can use an action to ignite it. At the end of each round, an unattended burning zone spreads to one adjacent unburned zone. Water, blankets, suitable magic, or another clearly effective method extinguishes a zone automatically; improvised methods require a {@dc 13} appropriate check.
The strike team withdraws if the Veteran falls, both oil carriers are stopped, or four of the seven members are out of the fight.
Even if all three ordinary archive zones burn, the sealed report beneath the Command Stone survives, preserving the essential Tyren/Unturned lead.

entries.name: Resting and Time Pressure
entries: A Short Rest is possible, but the keep and the incoming strike team continue moving.
Before the strike team arrives, an hour of rest lets it reach the island and begin setting up at the archive route.
After the strike team is known to be present, an hour gives it enough time to ignite unprotected archive zones and withdraw with whatever portable records it can carry.
Once the strike team is defeated or driven off and the old defenders are released, the keep becomes safe enough for a normal Short Rest.

entries.name: No Cause for Alarm Historical Beat
entries: Among ordinary civic papers is a public circular dated shortly before Bellweather’s fall:

{@b PUBLIC ASSURANCE:} Reports of erratic watch conduct and contradictory instructions remain isolated. Civic services continue under established authority. Residents are asked to disregard irresponsible rumors. {@b There is no cause for alarm.}
Let the repeated wording stand on its own.

entries.name: Resting and Time
entries: A Short Rest is possible, but the keep and the current-day strike team keep moving.
If the party rests before securing the archive, the strike team arrives during the hour and begins with one vulnerable record bundle already burning.
If the strike team has been defeated or driven away and the Command Stone is secure, the party can take a Short Rest without creating a new combat encounter.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: If the Command Stone is released or destroyed, the bound defenders cease their old duty. Bellweather can later secure the keep without asking the party to garrison it.
Wern sends a small records-and-security detail after the expedition. If the old defenders remain active, the island is marked restricted until their duty can be resolved.
Returning with the records changes the investigation.
Ulric accepts that the coordination is not merely a modern criminal innovation.

Wern begins treating the problem as an internal-security threat and advocates stronger emergency powers, more checkpoints, and tighter command discipline. His response is severe enough to be genuinely debatable.
Brann focuses on the Unturned and asks what made them different.
Perrin reacts carefully. He asks more questions about the term Tyren than he should logically need to, then catches himself.
If challenged, he explains that anyone hearing the report would want to understand the threat.

entries.name: DM Truth
entries: Perrin asks the Spirit about the name {@b Tyren} in private.
Tyren tells him that the old rulers feared the true spirit of Bellweather and branded it a threat because it could make the city act with one purpose.
Perrin does not fully believe this explanation.
He chooses to keep listening anyway.

Once the records are recovered, Council archivists and a small security detail take custody of the surviving archive. If the old defenders were released, Savin Keep becomes a quiet historical/military site rather than another permanent dungeon.

entries.name: Pepper: Mission 3 Complete
entries: Completing the mission marks {@b Mission 3 of 5}.

Lessa or Kav can be present when the recovered maps and records are logged. Their attitude should reflect what Pepper has actually done during the mandatory missions rather than reset to hostility every time.
Mission pay is {@b 75 gp per PC}.

entries.name: Milestone
entries: Remain {@b level 5}; Savin Keep combines with Cardon Weavehouse for the next milestone.

data.name: Chapter 8: Cardon Weavehouse

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/cardon_weavehouse.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/cardon_weavehouse.webp}
{@b Recommended level:} 5 {@b Expected milestone:} 6 {@b Likely table time:} 1–2 sessions

entries.name: Modern Running Sheet

rows: Let Perrin’s original dream visibly succeed: Cardon wealth and Bellweather prosperity begin returning together.
Recover Cardon and civic records, resolve current occupants/hostile holdouts, secure valuable machinery and assets.
Support Perrin’s claim, impose public conditions, negotiate with occupants, divide records/assets, or challenge ownership.
Family deeds, civic ledgers, worker testimony, and machinery records overlap. Losing one source changes the ownership hearing, not whether the Weavehouse story can continue.
Mission 4 of 5. All four PCs receive 75 gp each.
Perrin’s methods are producing visible good, making his rationalizations more persuasive to himself and to the city.

entries: {@i Use the existing Cardon Weavehouse map.}
{@b Site population:} 10 noncombatant workers/squatters and 5 armed holdouts.
{@b Armed roster:} 1 Gladiator leader, 2 Veterans, and 2 Scouts.
{@b Approach:} 1 Veteran + 1 Scout.
{@b Loom Hall:} Gladiator + 1 Veteran + 1 Scout.
{@b Morale:} the armed holdouts are protecting a payday, not a cause. They surrender or flee when the Gladiator falls or their exits remain open.

entries.name: Rewards and Treasure
entries: Council pay: {@b 75 gp per PC}.
Party salvage: 1 {@item Immovable Rod|XDMG}, 1 {@item Potion of Greater Healing|XDMG}, and 1 {@item Potion of Growth|XDMG}.
The sealed Cardon reserve is exactly {@b 2,500 gp equivalent} in coin, trade bars, gems, and negotiable records. It is disputed property, not automatic party loot.

entries.name: Why the Party Goes
entries: Savin’s records identify the Cardon Weavehouse as one of the sites where pre-fall emergency supply books, shipping ledgers, and old property archives were duplicated.
Perrin publicly asks the Council to authorize an expedition. His reasons are openly mixed:

items: the records may clarify the Tyren mystery;
surviving machinery could create jobs;
the building belongs to his family under old deeds;
restoring a major Cardon enterprise would bring capital into Bellweather.

entries: None of those claims is automatically false.
This is exactly why the chapter matters.

entries.name: Perrin’s Public Position
entries: Perrin does not hide that he wants his family property back.
He argues that Bellweather needs private investment, functioning businesses, and people willing to risk money on recovery. He promises to reopen the Weavehouse rather than leave it as a private ruin.
If the party challenges him on profiting from Council risk, he does not become sinister. He argues the point.

entries.name: 1. Approach
entries: The Weavehouse is occupied by a mixed group of squatters, hired guards, and opportunists using portions of the structure.
Separate people by behavior rather than species.

Some occupants will leave if offered safe passage. Some workers claim they have maintained machinery for years and deserve a share. A small armed faction intends to sell the contents and resists negotiation.
There are 10 noncombatant occupants in the site and 5 armed holdouts total.
{@b Deployment.} 1 Veteran and 1 Scout watch the main approach. They challenge intruders and retreat toward the Loom Hall if pressed; they do not fight to the death.
If the party offers safe passage before combat, half the noncombatants leave immediately and the remainder stay only to protect personal property or employment claims.

entries.name: 2. Loom Hall
entries: The main loom floor is dangerous because of weakened catwalks and partially functioning mechanisms.

{@b Broken catwalk.} The damaged section is obvious to anyone examining it. A creature that crosses it at speed makes a {@dc 14} Dexterity save or falls 20 feet, taking 2d6 bludgeoning damage and landing Prone.

{@b Suspended weights.} A character adjacent to a release can drop a weight as an action. A creature in the marked area makes a {@dc 14} Dexterity save, taking 3d6 bludgeoning damage on a failure or half on a success; the area becomes Difficult Terrain.

{@b Jammed gear train.} A creature shoved into the machinery makes a {@dc 14} Dexterity save or becomes Restrained. It or an adjacent creature can use an action to free it automatically once the mechanism is stopped; forcing it free while running requires a {@dc 14} Strength check.
{@b Dye spill.} Breaking or tipping the stored dyes creates a 15-foot slick. It is Difficult Terrain; a creature that Dashes through it makes a {@dc 13} Dexterity save or falls Prone.
{@b Encounter.} Gladiator leader + 2 Veterans + 2 Guards. They use catwalks and machinery but do not fight to the death.
{@b Encounter.} Gladiator leader + 1 Veteran + 1 Scout.

{@b Broken catwalk.} A cracked section is obvious to anyone examining the floor. Crossing it quickly requires a {@dc 13} Acrobatics check; failure causes a 15-foot fall for 1d6 bludgeoning damage and Prone.

{@b Suspended weights.} A character adjacent to a release line can use an action to drop a weight into a 10-foot-square area. Creatures there make a {@dc 13} Dexterity save, taking 2d6 bludgeoning damage and falling Prone on a failure, half damage and no Prone on a success.

{@b Jammed gear train.} A creature entering the marked machinery lane must succeed on a {@dc 13} Dexterity save or become Restrained by belts/gears. An adjacent creature can free it with an action and a {@dc 13} Strength check, suitable tools, or by stopping the mechanism.
{@b Stored dyes.} Spilling a vat creates a 10-foot-square area of Difficult Terrain. If ignited, creatures entering or ending a turn there take 1d6 fire damage until the fire is suppressed.

entries.name: 3. Worker Quarters
entries: Several current occupants are noncombatants who have been living in the building.
They know Cardon agents have already visited and offered employment if Perrin regains legal control.
Most of those offers are real.

This is one of the first visible examples of Perrin using influence for something that produces a genuinely positive result. People who were suspicious of him become enthusiastic after short private conversations.
PC saves do not occur here. The effect is on NPCs and should still look like charisma, hope, or politics.
Eight of the ten noncombatants normally sleep or store belongings here; two work around the Loom Hall. If combat starts nearby, they try to leave through the safest visible exit.

entries.name: 4. Family Archive
entries: The archive contains Cardon deeds, partnership papers, and proof that the family once held substantial legitimate property.
It also contains emergency ledgers showing that the Weavehouse supplied food, cloth, and shelter during the first days of the old crisis.
Perrin can point to this history as evidence that the Cardons did not merely enrich themselves; they helped hold the city together.
A separate civic ledger references transfers to Marren Library during the last week before the fall.
That is the next major historical lead.

The Cardon deeds and the civic transfer ledger are both recovered automatically once the archive is secured. A {@dc 14} Investigation check finds, in about one minute, the cross-reference showing the transfer to Marren Library; without the check, ten minutes of careful sorting reveals it.

entries.name: 5. Hidden Cardon Reserve
entries: A family reserve of portable wealth survived behind a sealed wall.
The reserve contains exactly {@b 2,400 gp equivalent} in coin, trade bars, gems, and negotiable records. It is subject to the ownership decision and is not automatic party loot.
Legally, most of it belongs to Perrin under the recognized deed unless the party or Council successfully challenges that claim.
Recovering it materially changes Perrin’s circumstances.
This is the point where the Cardon fortune stops being a nostalgic ambition and becomes real economic power.
An {@item Immovable Rod|XDMG} used as part of an old machinery-security system is released to the party as salvage after the site is documented.

entries.name: Resting and Site Response
entries: Before the armed holdouts are resolved, a Short Rest gives them an hour to barricade the Loom Hall, move portable valuables toward an exit, and warn any remaining lookout.
They do not gain new combatants. The same finite roster simply improves its position.
After the armed holdouts surrender or flee, the Weavehouse is safe enough for a Short Rest while workers, Council representatives, and Cardon agents begin documenting claims.

entries.name: The Ownership Decision
entries: The party does not decide Bellweather law by fiat, but its testimony and actions matter.
Possible outcomes include:

items: recognize Perrin’s full claim;
require compensation or tenancy rights for current workers;
place historical records in public custody while returning commercial assets to Perrin;
negotiate a mixed public/private operation;
challenge the claim and force a Council hearing.

entries: Perrin remembers how the party treats him here.
He does not need to become their enemy if they oppose him.

entries.name: Resting, Alert, and Aftermath
entries: If the outer patrol raises an alarm, the Loom Hall group gathers around the main floor while the eight noncombatants begin leaving through the safest worker exit.
A Short Rest before the armed group is resolved gives them time to bar two entrances, move portable valuables, and prepare the Loom Hall. It does not create extra defenders.

After the ownership decision, Council surveyors secure dangerous machinery and document the archive. If Perrin receives control, reopening begins over the following weeks. If the claim is contested, the building remains guarded while a hearing proceeds rather than resetting into another dungeon.

entries.name: Bellweather Changes
entries: Immediately after the expedition, the Council posts a property notice and keeps the machinery from being stripped while the ownership question is resolved.
The party is not expected to guard the Weavehouse. Workers and hired security take over once a legal operating arrangement exists.
Within weeks, if Perrin receives enough of the property, the Weavehouse reopens in some form.
Jobs appear.
Merchants invest.
The Cardon name becomes associated with visible recovery.
Perrin’s wealth and public approval increase together.
This is a success story.
That fact is essential to his corruption.

entries.name: DM Truth: Rewarding the Hidden Desire
entries: Tyren’s gift appears vindicated.

Perrin can now look at a functioning business, paid workers, increasing trade, and restored family wealth and conclude that his willingness to do what cautious people would not do is exactly why Bellweather is improving.
The hidden desire for power is no longer merely hidden. Perrin begins enjoying being the person who can make outcomes happen.

entries.name: Pepper: Mission 4 Complete
entries: Mark {@b Mission 4 of 5 complete} when the authorized objective is resolved and Pepper returns as required.
Mission pay is {@b 75 gp per PC}.

entries.name: Milestone
entries: Advance to {@b level 6} after the Savin Keep + Cardon Weavehouse arc is resolved.

data.name: Chapter 9: Marren Library

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/marren_library.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/marren_library.webp}
{@b Recommended level:} 6 {@b Expected milestone:} 7 after the Marren/Mansion phase {@b Likely table time:} 1–2 sessions

entries.name: Modern Running Sheet

rows: Reveal what Tyren can do without yet revealing what Tyren physically is. Finish Pepper’s five-mission Council sentence.
Preserve the archive, recover the Tyren material, stop a targeted theft/burning of records, decide who controls copies.
Work with scholars, Council, Cardon interests, or independent custodians; split priorities; protect records rather than simply clear rooms.

The Tyren journal, Unturned file, property archive, and catalog record are physically separated. Fire, theft, or a failed ward check can cost secondary material but cannot erase the core possession/Radiant Cage revelation.
Mission 5 of 5. All four PCs receive 75 gp each. Completing the mission ends Pepper’s mandatory service and house arrest.
Tyren can occupy living hosts; the Radiant Well was used to contain him; killing a host does not necessarily kill Tyren.

entries: {@i Use the existing Marren Library map and archive geography.}
{@b Finite hostile roster:} 2 Gargoyles at the Garden Court if disturbed, 1 Spy + 3 Thugs removing selected books in the Damaged Stacks, and 2 Animated Armors guarding the research wing.
{@b Library staff:} 3 living staff members are trapped or endangered in the Damaged Stacks.
{@b No random encounter stack:} the listed threats are the whole expected hostile population for the chapter unless actual play creates a new problem.

entries.name: Rewards and Treasure
entries: Council pay: {@b 75 gp per PC}.
Utility item: 1 {@item Eyes of Minute Seeing|XDMG}.
Spell scrolls: {@spell Lesser Restoration}, {@spell Locate Object}, and {@spell Protection from Evil and Good}.
Secondary manuscripts are worth up to {@b 500 gp}; each archive zone lost to fire reduces that sale value by 125 gp.

rows: Garden Court, only if monument disturbed

entries.name: Why the Party Goes
entries: The Savin records and Cardon Weavehouse ledgers independently point to Marren Library as the institution that received sealed magical research during the final week before Old Bellweather fell.
The Council needs the archive before somebody else removes the same material.
Pepper’s fifth mandatory job is therefore not a punishment invented around her. It is a legitimate Council mission that happens to complete her sentence.

entries.name: Competing Interests
entries: Three interests arrive at once:
{@b Council clerks} want dangerous historical records kept in public custody.
{@b Scholars} want damaged collections stabilized and copied before politics decides ownership.
{@b Perrin} wants Cardon family papers returned to him and argues that private records should not become permanent Council property simply because they survived in a public archive.
Perrin’s legal position is not automatically unreasonable.

entries.name: 1. Garden Court
entries: The overgrown court contains signs of recent passage.
Exactly 2 Gargoyles animate only if the central monument is disturbed. Otherwise the court is an investigation scene.
Someone arrived first looking for the same material.

entries.name: 2. Damaged Stacks
entries: A fire is already burning in the magical-research wing while the scavenger team removes selected volumes.
{@b Starting positions.} The Veteran and 1 Thug hold the central aisle. The second Thug feeds the fire. The 2 Spies each begin with a selected volume and move toward separate exits.

{@b Fire clock.} Three archive sections are at risk. At initiative count 20, one uncontrolled burning section spreads to the next unburned section. A character adjacent to a burning section can extinguish it with an action using water, blankets, appropriate magic, or another obviously effective method. An uncertain improvised method uses a {@dc 13} appropriate check.

If all three sections are allowed to burn, contextual records are lost, but the essential Tyren file in the warded chamber survives. Each saved section preserves additional names, dates, and corroborating evidence.

A trapped junior archivist is behind the second threatened section. Reaching and escorting the archivist to safety takes one character's movement and action unless a spell or equally effective solution changes that.
The scavengers were paid through an anonymous Covenant-style drop and know only the shelf numbers and subjects they were told to retrieve.
{@b Hostiles.} 1 Spy directs 3 Thugs who are removing selected volumes. Their priority is books and escape, not killing the party.
{@b Staff.} Three library staff are endangered: one pinned by a fallen shelf, one cut off by smoke, and one trapped behind the thieves near the research stair.

{@b Fire track.} Divide the damaged stacks into four archive zones. One zone is burning when the party arrives. At the end of each round, if no progress was made against the fire that round, it spreads into one adjacent unburned zone.

Three successful fire-control actions contain the fire. Water, a suitable spell, closing a fire door, or another clearly effective method counts automatically. An improvised method requires a {@dc 13} appropriate check.

Freeing the pinned staff member requires an action and either a {@dc 13} Athletics check or a clearly sufficient tool/spell. Reaching the smoke-cut-off staff member safely requires protection from the smoke, a quick route, or a {@dc 13} Survival/Investigation check to identify the safest path.
The essential Tyren journal and Unturned file are in protected rooms and cannot be destroyed by this stacks fire. Each of the four secondary zones lost reduces recoverable manuscript value by 125 gp.

entries.name: 3. Master Librarian’s Chamber
entries: A damaged ward protects a locked desk. A {@dc 15} Intelligence (Arcana) check or {@spell Dispel Magic} suppresses it. On a failed Arcana check, the character makes a {@dc 14} Wisdom save; on a failure the character is Frightened until the end of its next turn. The desk and clue remain recoverable.

{@b Warded corridor defenders.} 2 Animated Armors and 2 Flying Swords animate when the party passes the suppressed ward toward the sealed research stacks. They stop fighting if the ward is lawfully deactivated with the librarian's recovered key phrase or if the constructs are defeated.

The ward can be suppressed with a {@dc 15} Arcana check, a {@dc 15} check using thieves’ tools after its mechanism is studied, or {@spell Dispel Magic}. On a failed check, the character makes a {@dc 14} Wisdom save or is Frightened until the end of their next turn; the desk remains accessible for another attempt.
Inside are several damaged records that finally make the supernatural problem explicit.

entries.name: Essential Record: Tyren
entries: The clearest surviving journal says, in careful academic language, that {@b Tyren is an intelligence capable of occupying living hosts}.
It does not identify Tyren’s species.
The author believed:

items: Tyren’s influence could spread through repeated psychic contact;
some people were unusually resistant;
destroying a controlled host would not necessarily destroy Tyren;
the Radiant Well was used in the final containment;
the containment was called the {@b Radiant Cage} in technical notes.

entries: A margin note reads:
{@b The Cage is not a tomb. It is a return. They forced him back into himself.}
The 2 Animated Armors activate only if the ward is violently broken or the research wing is entered after the thieves raise an alarm. They do not appear as extra reinforcements elsewhere.

entries.name: 4. The Unturned File
entries: A separate file contains testimonies about resistant people.
The testimonies disagree about why resistance occurred. Some resistant people were devout. Some were traumatized veterans. Some were children. Some were ordinary people with no obvious shared trait.
The archivist’s conclusion is deliberately uncertain:
{@b “The common quality may not be strength of mind. It may be certainty of self.”}
This is the historical foundation for the anchored-mind rule.
The file never identifies which PCs qualify or why.

No check is required to identify the repeated resistance pattern once the file is read. A {@dc 14} Insight, History, or Religion check adds that the accounts describe stable identity/conviction rather than one shared spell, bloodline, or institution.

entries.name: 5. Property Archives
entries: Perrin’s family materials are here as well.
They confirm that the Cardons were among Bellweather’s founders and that their wealth was heavily damaged during the original fall.
They also show that emergency powers transferred property, contracts, and civic obligations in ways that were never fully resolved.
Perrin is especially attentive to these records.
The party may give him originals, copies, or require public duplication first.
The Cardon material is indexed. Ten minutes of review finds the major deeds automatically; a {@dc 14} Investigation check finds the unresolved emergency-transfer language in one minute.

entries.name: 6. The Missing Volume
entries: One volume is gone before the party arrives.
Its catalog entry describes it only as:
{@b VAREN CONTAINMENT — PHYSICAL FORM / LOWER CHAMBER}
This preserves the dragon reveal.
The missing volume has been taken by Tyren-controlled agents through the criminal network because it contains too much information about the body beneath Varen Keep.
The party cannot recover it here.

entries.name: Resting, Time, and Archive Aftermath
entries: The party can take a Short Rest only after deciding what happens to the active fire and scavenger team. If they wait an hour while either remains unresolved, the thieves escape with their selected books and the unprotected archive sections are lost.
Once the fire is contained and the hostile team is gone, a Short Rest is safe inside the library.

After the mission, scholars and Council clerks secure the surviving archive, make duplicate copies of dangerous records, and begin stabilizing the building. The missing Varen volume remains missing by design and points onward rather than representing a failed search.

entries.name: Resting and Time Pressure
entries: A Short Rest while the stacks fire is unresolved allows the fire to consume every unprotected secondary archive zone and lets surviving thieves leave with whatever selected books they still carry.
A Short Rest after the fire is contained is possible, but surviving thieves or outside claimants continue moving; the party may return to find custody representatives already present.
No rest can erase the protected Tyren journal, Unturned file, or missing-volume catalog entry.

entries.name: Perrin’s Reaction
entries: When the party discusses Tyren and possession, Perrin’s reaction should be controlled but imperfect.
He is disturbed.

He has been calling this presence the Spirit of the City for years. The records tell him that an entity with the same kind of influence was trapped beneath Varen Keep after nearly destroying Bellweather.
He asks whether old frightened officials could have misunderstood a protective spirit.
This is not a calculated lie. He wants that answer to be true.

entries.name: DM Truth: Perrin Chooses the Comfortable Explanation
entries: Tyren tells Perrin that the old ruling class feared a force capable of making Bellweather act together and imprisoned the city’s true spirit to preserve their own authority.
Perrin now has enough evidence to walk away.
He does not.
By this point the Spirit’s power has restored his family’s fortune, expanded employment, and made Perrin one of Bellweather’s most effective public figures.
Perrin decides the old records are incomplete and biased.
This is a choice.

entries.name: Custody Decision
entries: The party decides who receives the most dangerous records and copies.
Possible custodians include:

items: the Council archive;
Marren scholars;
Bishop Brann’s religious institution;
Perrin for Cardon-specific records only;
multiple copies split among institutions.

entries: Brakkus, if consulted later, strongly favors {@b redundancy}. His concern is practical: no single person should be able to make dangerous knowledge disappear.

entries.name: Pepper: Mission 5 Complete
entries: Successful completion of this assignment marks {@b Mission 5 of 5}.
Pepper has fulfilled the Council’s sentence.
Her mandatory mission obligation and Ledger House arrest end. She is no longer required to continue adventuring for the Council.

Lessa Dorn and Kav Orin can be present when the final field documentation is accepted. Their role pays off here: they were among the people who reported the original accusation, and they have now also seen Pepper complete the work imposed on her.
Reconciliation is not assumed. Their attitude depends on what Pepper actually did during the five missions.
Pepper’s later encounter with Caleb’s family is {@b not part of the sentence} and is not another punishment.
Mission pay is {@b 75 gp per PC}.
Once the final paperwork is accepted, Pepper is no longer under house arrest and has no compulsory Council jobs remaining.

entries.name: Library Aftermath
entries: After the expedition, scholars and Council clerks establish a guarded records room rather than leaving the party to protect the building.

If the party preserved most of the stacks, the library resumes limited public work quickly. If much of the secondary archive burned, reconstruction and copying take longer, but the core Tyren evidence still reaches the investigation.
The custody decision determines where originals and copies go; it does not require the party to remain on site.

entries.name: Milestone
entries: Advance to {@b level 7} once Marren Library and the associated Mansion/Cardon consequences are meaningfully resolved.

data.name: Interlude: Caleb’s Family
entries: Run this after Marren Library and before or during the next Bellweather-focused arc, when there is enough table space for the scene to matter.

entries.name: Kerrik Brings the News
entries: Use the full NPC profiles in {@b Core Recurring Cast}. This scene works best if Kerrik, Mara, and Elise feel like people with conflicting needs rather than instruments for Pepper's character development.
{@b Kerrik}, an aarakocra and Caleb’s closest friend, comes to Ledger House looking specifically for Pepper.
He knows what the Council concluded about Caleb’s death.
He is not there to arrest Pepper, threaten her, or extend the sentence.
He tells her that Caleb’s daughter, {@b Elise}, is seriously ill and ordinary healing has not fixed it.
Kerrik does not like asking Pepper for anything. He is doing it because Caleb’s widow has run out of options and Pepper is a cleric with access to stronger magic.

entries.name: Mara and Elise
entries: {@b Mara} is human, angry, exhausted, and direct.
She does not forgive Pepper because Pepper arrived with healing magic.
Her request is emotionally simple:
{@b “You killed my husband. I know what the Council says happened. I also know you are a cleric, and my daughter is sick. Help her.”}
Mara’s request remains separate from Council terms, reputation, payment, alignment, and future quests.
Pepper may help or refuse.
That choice belongs to the player.

entries.name: Elise’s Affliction
entries: Elise is not possessed and Tyren did not deliberately target her.
Her illness is {@b psychic spillover} from the expanding network Tyren has built through influenced people in Bellweather.
Symptoms can include:

items: severe headaches;
insomnia;
brief fugue states;
answering questions nobody asked aloud;
beginning a simple action and then stopping, confused about why she started;
repeating a phrase heard elsewhere in the network.

entries: Ordinary healing restores hit points but does not remove the condition.
Treat the affliction as a supernatural mental curse/possession residue removable by {@b Greater Restoration} or equivalent story-appropriate high magic.
If Pepper uses {@i Greater Restoration}, Elise recovers.
The spell also reveals something useful: for a moment, Pepper senses that the affliction was not rooted inside Elise. It was pressure {@b passing through} her from somewhere else.
That makes the family scene a personal clue without making Caleb’s murder part of Tyren’s plan.

data.name: Chapter 10: The Mansion District
entries: {@b Recommended level:} 6–7 {@b Milestone:} Shared with Marren Library; none for clearing houses {@b Likely table time:} optional / merged material

entries.name: Table-Ready Optional Side Adventures
Legitimate Inheritance
entries: A returning family offers {@b 500 gp total} to recover heirlooms from a structurally unsafe mansion now occupied by three peaceful tenant families.
The danger is inside the sealed vault: 2 Animated Armors and 1 Mimic. The tenants are not enemies and have a legitimate claim to relocation/compensation if displaced.
A {@dc 14} Investigation check finds the old maintenance plan quickly; ten minutes of careful searching finds it automatically. The plan gives a safe route around the collapsed stair.
The heirlooms belong to the family. The party's meaningful decision is how it reports the tenants' interests.

entries.name: Fraudulent Claim
entries: A polished claimant offers {@b 400 gp total} to recover a deed chest. The claimant is a Spy with 1 Veteran and 2 Thugs posing as hired security.
Correctly comparing the claimant's papers with public property marks exposes a mismatch automatically. A {@dc 14} Investigation check notices the mismatch immediately before entering the house.
The deed chest is protected by a visible old needle plate: {@dc 14} thieves' tools to disable; triggering it causes a {@dc 14} Constitution save, 2d6 poison damage on a failure or half on a success.
If exposed, the claimant bargains or flees; the hired muscle does not fight once the fraud is public and payment is clearly gone.

entries.name: Public Promise
entries: A recovered deed proves that one wealthy estate permanently dedicated its walled garden to a hospice, school, shrine, or public garden. Modern heirs want the mansion but contest the public-use clause.
The clause is genuine and requires no check once the original deed is recovered. The physical obstacle is a sealed garden watched by 2 Gargoyles and a collapsed gate.
The gate can be opened with a {@dc 14} Athletics check, appropriate tools, or ten minutes of careful clearing without a roll.
The Council pays {@b 300 gp total} for recovering and authenticating the deed. The lasting reward is civic influence, not additional treasure.
Clearing optional Mansion District material never grants a level by itself.

entries.name: Purpose
entries: The Mansion District survives as a major named part of Bellweather, but it is no longer a mandatory reclamation chapter.
Use it for private commissions, inheritance conflicts, hidden vaults, social consequences of Perrin’s rise, and side adventures when the players choose to engage with wealthy families or old records.
The district is valuable because it shows Bellweather becoming prosperous {@b without every problem being Tyren}.
This material is optional. It is not required for campaign progression, but each model below is ready to use as a one-session side adventure if the players choose the district.

entries.name: Perrin in the District
entries: Perrin becomes increasingly influential among returning families and investors.
He does not have to control everyone he persuades.
Some people support him because:

items: he restored a major business;
he has money;
he gets things done;
he is charismatic;
his policies benefit them.

entries: Use supernatural influence sparingly here. The point is that Perrin no longer needs magic for every victory.

entries.name: Story Use
entries: The Mansion District can provide:

items: Cardon family history;
old civic correspondence;
wealthy political allies;
evidence of how much Perrin’s social standing has changed;
unrelated treasure hunts and monster encounters;
a place where players can choose to oppose, support, or negotiate with returning wealth.

entries: Clearing houses by itself does not award a milestone.

data.name: Chapter 11: Paden Square

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/paden_square.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/paden_square.webp}
{@b Recommended level:} 7 {@b Milestone:} None by itself {@b Likely table time:} 1–2 sessions

entries.name: Modern Running Sheet

rows: Show Tyren controlling a large group at once and introduce the first Command-level pressure on the PCs without pointing directly at Perrin.
Protect civilians, identify why supposedly separate groups move together, stop a coordinated seizure of the square, preserve evidence.
Infiltration, staged trade, crowd management, rooftop approach, negotiation, sabotage, or direct combat.
The mass-control event happens visibly enough that the party can investigate it even if leaders escape.
Tyren can move a crowd like one organism. Anchored minds resist differently.

entries: {@i Use the existing Paden Square map and marketplace layout.}
{@b Finite active hostile roster:} 1 {@creature Veteran|XMM} field leader, 2 additional Veterans, and 4 Scouts.
{@b Civilian map pieces:} use 4 civilian clusters, not individual NPC hit-point pools. Each cluster represents several shoppers/workers trapped by the synchronized movement.
{@b Starting positions:} field leader + 1 Veteran at the central wagon; 1 Veteran at the east exit; 2 Scouts on rooftops; 1 Scout with the wagon; 1 Scout is the courier at the center of the square.
{@b Tyren pressure:} PC/Jord Wisdom save DC is {@dc 14}. Failure uses only the established one-turn Command ceiling.

entries.name: Rewards and Treasure
entries: Recovered criminal payments and contraband total {@b 750 gp}.
The field leader also carries 1 {@item Potion of Heroism|XDMG}; the courier satchel contains 1 {@item Potion of Greater Healing|XDMG}.
The larger rewards are public credibility, evidence, and changed Council relationships.

entries.name: The Setup
entries: Paden Square is functioning as a busy commercial center again.

Perrin sees an opportunity to accelerate his political strategy. Through surviving criminal intermediaries, he encourages several crews to stage thefts, intimidation, and a public failure of security during a crowded market day.
His intended sequence is cynical but limited:

items: visible disorder embarrasses the Council;
Wern responds too aggressively;
Perrin argues for competent unified leadership;
Perrin supports a crackdown and earns public trust.

entries: Tyren hijacks the event.

entries.name: 1. Market Tension
entries: Begin with ordinary problems: pickpockets, nervous guards, rival merchants, rumors that the Council cannot keep the square safe.
The scene begins as ordinary public tension; supernatural behavior appears later.
The party may learn that several groups known to dislike each other are present at the same time.

entries.name: 2. The Trigger
entries: At a chosen moment, the square changes.
Several criminals stop whatever they are doing and look in the same direction.
Then they move.
No shouted order passes between them.
Some civilians also begin performing simple coordinated actions: closing shutters, blocking exits, moving carts, or walking toward preselected positions.
The movements are not tactically perfect. They are unnaturally unified.

entries.name: 3. First Anchored-Mind Saves
entries: This is the recommended first use of unexplained Tyren saves on the PCs.
Ask each PC for a {@dc 14} Wisdom saving throw when the pressure reaches the whole square.
Describe only the Wisdom save unless the characters have already established that language through play.
On a failure, use one brief Command-like imperative appropriate to the scene:

items: {@b Halt} — the character spends the turn unable to advance;
{@b Drop} — the character drops one held nonessential object;
{@b Flee} — the character uses movement to get away from the center of the square;
{@b Approach} — the character moves toward a marked point or doorway;
{@b Yield} — the character steps aside and allows someone to pass.

entries: The compelled action never forces an attack, spell expenditure, consumable use, or irreversible action.
The player has full control immediately afterward.
Jord, if present, can also make the save and may fail in a mildly comic but useful way: he starts following an imperative, catches himself, and angrily asks who agreed to these terms.

entries.name: 4. The Unturned Pattern Reappears
entries: Bishop Brann, if present in the square or brought into the aftermath, is unaffected.
Brakkus is also unaffected if circumstances place him nearby.
Let the immunity emerge through contrast rather than announcement. Let the contrast exist.
A character who compares the event to Marren’s Unturned records has enough information to form the hypothesis that some people are harder for Tyren to seize.

entries.name: 5. Combat and Objectives
entries: Use exactly 1 Veteran field leader, 2 Veterans, and 4 Scouts. The controlled civilians are terrain/objective pieces, not enemies.

{@b Courier.} One Scout begins at the center carrying the most useful written evidence. On its first turn it Dashes toward the south exit. If it escapes, the same basic Covenant instructions can still be recovered from the field leader, but the party loses the clearest delivery trail.

{@b Wagon blockade.} At initiative count 20 on rounds 1 and 2, the controlled wagon advances toward the west exit unless a character reaches the driver/harness and uses an action to stop it. Once the exit is blocked, moving the wagon quickly requires a {@dc 14} Strength (Athletics) check or an obviously effective spell/tool solution.

{@b Civilian clusters.} Four civilian clusters begin in exposed areas. At initiative count 20, one unprotected cluster moves 15 feet toward the nearest marked danger/blockade under Tyren's pressure. A character adjacent to a cluster can use an action to guide it to safety automatically; a spell or strong plan can protect multiple clusters if it logically would.
{@b Enemy jobs.} The field leader protects the central documents; one Veteran helps the wagon blockade; one Veteran holds an exit; rooftop Scouts pressure characters who leave cover.

The fight ends as an organized operation when the field leader falls/surrenders, the courier is stopped or escapes, and at least two exits are open. Surviving criminals then flee, surrender, or wake from the synchronized state.

entries.name: Resting, Withdrawal, and Fail-Forward
entries: The market crisis does not pause for a Short Rest. The party can withdraw for an hour, but the event resolves while they are gone.

If they leave before stabilizing the square, the courier escapes, the west exit is blocked, and two civilian clusters suffer injuries before guards/merchants regain control. The party can still investigate the aftermath and recover ordinary Covenant instructions.

rows: Field-leader documents and witness accounts still prove organized Covenant disorder.
Surviving criminals and written instructions establish the same facts.
Multiple surviving criminals independently describe the same impossible synchronization.
Public trust rises; the investigation continues through witnesses rather than the courier.

entries.name: 6. The Evidence
entries: The criminals carried ordinary Covenant instructions for disorder.
Those instructions do {@b not} explain the mass synchronization.
Surviving criminals are as frightened as anyone else. Several insist they remember deciding to move but cannot explain why.
One says:
{@b “It felt like I’d already decided before I knew there was a choice.”}
That sentence should matter later.

After the crisis, the square closes for the rest of the day. By the next morning it reopens with damaged stalls, temporary guard posts, and merchants loudly arguing about what happened rather than accepting one official explanation.

entries.name: Perrin’s Reaction
entries: Perrin publicly condemns the disorder and supports relief for merchants and civilians.
He privately understands exactly what he saw: the Spirit took the network Perrin built and moved it as one body.
This is the clearest warning he has received.

entries.name: DM Truth: Perrin’s Greatest Off-Ramp
entries: Perrin now knows that the Spirit can override groups directly.
He knows the old records described exactly this kind of event.
He knows people were hurt.
He could expose the bargain, surrender his political future, and ask Brann or the party for help.
He chooses not to.
The reason is no longer ignorance.
Part of him is horrified.
Part of him is impressed.

entries.name: Wern’s Response
entries: Wern advocates emergency measures: controlled entry points, more armed patrols, temporary curfews around vulnerable markets, and a unified chain of command.
Some of these measures are defensible. Some are excessive.
Perrin does not need to fabricate Wern’s severity. He simply lets people see it and positions himself as the calm alternative.

entries.name: No Cause for Alarm Beat
entries: Perrin addresses merchants and residents after the crisis.
He acknowledges the attack, praises the response, and insists Bellweather remains strong.
He ends with a familiar civic reassurance:
{@b “We will not hand this city back to fear. Bellweather is open, Bellweather is growing, and there is no cause for alarm.”}
This is the first time the phrase should feel deliberately political.

entries.name: Milestone
entries: Remain {@b level 7}; Paden Square and Storen Gate form the next milestone.

data.name: Chapter 12: Storen Gate

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/storen_gate.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/storen_gate.webp}
{@b Recommended level:} 7 {@b Expected milestone:} 8 {@b Likely table time:} 1–2 sessions

entries.name: Modern Running Sheet

rows: Give Perrin the first situation in which he knowingly asks Tyren to directly control someone because persuasion feels too slow.
Resolve a genuine security crisis at the gate, prevent outside forces from exploiting Bellweather’s instability, identify compromised orders.
Defend, infiltrate, negotiate, sabotage signals, evacuate civilians, or expose false orders.
Failure changes control of sections of the gate and creates casualties; it does not end the campaign.
Direct control can solve a real problem, which becomes Perrin’s justification for using it voluntarily.

entries: {@i Use the existing Storen Gate map and strategic gate terrain.}
{@b Gate garrison present:} 1 Knight officer and 6 Guards. They are allies/neutral personnel unless the party turns the crisis into a fight with them.
{@b Finite hostile infiltration force:} 1 {@creature Gladiator|XMM}, 2 Veterans, and 4 Scouts.
{@b Starting hostile positions:} Gladiator + 1 Veteran + 2 Scouts hidden among the relief wagons; 1 Veteran + 2 Scouts outside the gate waiting for the mechanism to open.
{@b Tyren pressure:} any anchored PC caught in the psychic pulse makes a {@dc 14} Wisdom save and is subject only to the one-turn Command ceiling.

entries.name: Rewards and Treasure
entries: Council pay is {@b 150 gp per character}.
The city also issues the party 1 {@item Immovable Rod|XDMG} from the gate engineering stores and 2 {@item Potion of Greater Healing|XDMG|Potions of Greater Healing}.
The main long-term reward is authority and trust earned through how the party resolves the gate crisis.

rows: Gate garrison, only if somehow fought

entries.name: The Crisis
entries: Storen Gate is not attacked because “the next district needs reclaiming.”

The crisis develops because Bellweather’s recent instability has become visible beyond the city. A hostile force, smuggling coalition, or armed regional faction tests the gate at the same time Wern has concentrated guards elsewhere after Paden Square.
The threat is real.
If the party does nothing, people may die and Bellweather may lose a critical route.

entries.name: 1. Conflicting Orders
entries: When the party arrives, the gate garrison has received contradictory instructions.
One order says hold the gate closed.
Another says admit a relief convoy.
Both appear to carry legitimate Council authorization.
Ulric’s office insists only one was issued.
Wern’s officers accuse civilian clerks of interference.
The confusion echoes Savin’s historical records without duplicating them exactly.

Both documents are physically authentic. Ten minutes comparing logs reveals that the relief order was entered during a clerk's unexplained memory gap. A {@dc 14} Investigation check finds that discrepancy immediately. Failure costs time; it does not make one document magically look fake.

entries.name: 2. The Relief Convoy
entries: The approaching convoy contains a mix of legitimate supplies and hostile infiltrators.
The party can discover the problem through inspection, scouts, magic, captured messengers, or simply watching who responds strangely to signals.
Discovery does not hinge on one roll; checks affect speed, detail, or cost.

entries.name: 3. Perrin’s Choice
entries: Perrin is at or near the gate because the crisis has become political as well as military.
At a critical point, an officer refuses a risky order Perrin believes is necessary to prevent the infiltrators from seizing the mechanism.
Perrin has alternatives:

items: persuade the officer;
defer to Wern;
let the party handle it;
accept the delay.

entries: Instead, in private thought, Perrin asks the Spirit for help.
Tyren takes the officer.
The officer immediately obeys.
The decision works.
Lives are saved because the gate moves at exactly the right moment.
This is the first time Perrin {@b knowingly requests direct control} rather than merely accepting influence or covering up Tyren’s independent action.

entries.name: 4. The Party’s View
entries: The moment is subtle enough to support more than one immediate interpretation.
The officer may simply change their mind abruptly.
Characters watching closely can notice:

items: a momentary blankness;
the officer using wording unlike their normal speech;
immediate obedience after refusing seconds earlier;
no visible conversation with Perrin.

entries: A {@dc 14} Insight check confirms that the officer's abrupt change is unnatural, but it does not identify Perrin or Tyren as the source.
If an anchored PC is caught in the same psychic pulse, call for a {@dc 14} Wisdom save and use the established one-turn Command ceiling.

entries.name: 5. Gate Fight
entries: {@b Portcullis.} Raising or lowering it normally takes two character actions at the winch. A character can force the mechanism through in one action with a {@dc 15} Strength (Athletics) check. Appropriate magic or sabotage can change this.

{@b Signal.} A character adjacent to the signal mechanism can disable it with an action and a {@dc 14} check using thieves' tools or appropriate artisan's tools. Destroying the exposed signal rope/lever also works automatically if the character can reach it.
{@b Hostile force.} Use exactly 1 Gladiator, 2 Veterans, and 4 Scouts. The hidden wagon group moves when the gate begins opening; the outside group rushes the mechanism once there is a gap.

{@b Garrison.} The Knight officer and 6 Guards protect workers/civilians and follow whichever legitimate command chain the party establishes. Do not add them to the hostile roster unless the party actually turns them against itself.

{@b Victory conditions.} The party wins by any combination that prevents the infiltrators from taking the mechanism, keeps the gate functional, and prevents a hostile signal from bringing in further opportunists. Killing every infiltrator is not required.

entries.name: Time, Rest, and Failure
entries: The active gate crisis does not wait through a Short Rest. If the party withdraws for an hour before resolving it, the infiltrators make their attempt without them.

If the party leaves before identifying the mixed convoy, the infiltrators seize part of the mechanism and several guards/workers are injured before Wern's reinforcements retake it. The party can still arrive for the aftermath and uncover the contradictory-order/control evidence.

rows: The gate is damaged and trade closes for several days; the campaign continues.
Captured scouts/records still identify the planned infiltration.
Other witnesses saw the unnatural reversal; Perrin's choice still happened.
Party exposes the order problem early
The final fight becomes easier because the garrison remains coordinated.

entries.name: 6. Aftermath
entries: The city celebrates a real victory.
Perrin can point to the gate and know, truthfully, that his decision saved people.
That is the danger.

entries.name: DM Truth: The New Rationalization
entries: Perrin’s internal argument becomes:
{@b If I had refused to use the power because of abstract moral fear, people would have died.}
He has now crossed from covering up Tyren’s behavior to {@b choosing direct control as a tool}.
The next time will be easier.
After the crisis, the gate remains under Bellweather control. Repairs, extra inspection points, and political arguments about emergency authority become visible immediately.

entries.name: Council Fracture
entries: Wern demands broader emergency authority after the gate crisis.
Ulric insists emergency power must remain documented, temporary, and reviewable.
Brann warns that fear does not make consent irrelevant.
Perrin positions himself between them, publicly rejecting both paralysis and overreaction.
His popularity increases.

entries.name: Milestone
entries: Advance to {@b level 8} after the Paden Square + Storen Gate escalation is resolved.

data.name: Chapter 13: Valen Cemetery

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/valen_cemetery.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/valen_cemetery.webp}
{@b Recommended level:} 8 {@b Milestone:} None by itself {@b Likely table time:} 1–2 sessions (optional)

entries.name: Modern Running Sheet

rows: Give the campaign a major problem that is not secretly Tyren, deepen Bishop Brann, and let the party observe true immunity without turning it into exposition.
Protect mourners and nearby residents, stop an undead outbreak, identify and destroy the necromantic source.
Research burial records, work with Brann, enter by daylight, use holy support, stealth, or direct cleansing.
Core lore about the undead source comes from multiple graves, witnesses, and ritual sites.
Brann is not merely resistant; Tyren cannot seize him at all.

entries: {@i Use the existing Valen Cemetery map and burial geography.}
{@b Finite undead roster:} 1 {@creature Wraith|XMM}, 2 Wights, 4 Ghouls, and 2 Specters.
{@b Memorial Walk:} 2 Ghouls + 1 Specter and 3 civilian clusters.
{@b Broken Mausoleum:} 2 Ghouls + 1 Specter.
{@b Necromantic Focus:} 1 Wraith + 2 Wights.
{@b Tyren probe:} if used, PC Wisdom save DC is {@dc 14}; Brann is immune.

entries.name: Rewards and Treasure
entries: The temple/cemetery fund pays {@b 400 gp total}.
Brann also provides 1 {@item Potion of Heroism|XDMG} and 2 {@item Potion of Greater Healing|XDMG|Potions of Greater Healing} from emergency stores.
The larger reward is temple/civic favor and the public evidence of Brann's immunity.

entries.name: Independent Threat
entries: The undead crisis at Valen Cemetery is {@b not caused by Tyren}.
Keep that boundary.
A damaged necromantic focus, restless dead, grave robbery, or an old funerary working has begun producing undead and endangering people who use the cemetery.
The campaign needs problems that matter even when Perrin and Tyren are not responsible.

entries.name: Bishop Brann’s Role
entries: Brann asks the party for help because this is his area of responsibility and because ordinary mourners are being endangered.
He should be useful without becoming the adventuring party’s combat solution.
He can:

items: provide burial records;
identify old rites;
protect civilians;
consecrate a safe staging area;
explain what kind of undead the party is facing;
perform a ritual while the PCs handle the dangerous part.

entries.name: 1. Memorial Walk
entries: Begin with an ordinary burial or reinterment involving 3 civilian clusters: mourners near the grave, workers by the path, and a family near the memorial wall.
The first outbreak is 2 Ghouls + 1 Specter. The undead are trying to reach living people, not hold an arena.

At initiative count 20, one unprotected civilian cluster is forced to move or scatter toward danger. A character adjacent to a cluster can use an action to guide it behind cover/safety automatically; a sensible spell or plan can protect more than one.
Brann focuses on keeping civilians alive and opening a safe route. He does not take over the party's combat.

entries.name: 2. Broken Mausoleum
entries: The disturbance traces to old underground burial chambers.
Clues point toward a cracked ritual focus and grave robbers who disturbed material they did not understand.
The robbers may still be alive and terrified. They are criminals, not Tyren agents.
{@b Encounter.} 2 Ghouls + 1 Specter are drawn to the cracked ritual material. Terrified grave robbers, if encountered, surrender immediately and can explain what they disturbed.

entries.name: 3. The Control Pulse
entries: During the investigation, Tyren takes advantage of the party being together and attempts a brief psychic pressure from afar.
This is not the cause of the undead. It is Tyren probing the people who survived Paden.
If the moment adds tension, call for a {@dc 14} Wisdom save from each PC. On a failure, use the established one-turn Command ceiling.
On a failure, use the established one-turn Command ceiling.
Brann is unaffected.
If a character watches Brann during the pulse, there is no blankness, hesitation, or struggle. He notices the pressure but it does not move him.

entries.name: 4. Brann’s Anchor
entries: Brann does not volunteer his childhood trauma unless trust and context lead him there.
If the party asks why he seems different from them, or if a quiet scene naturally opens the subject, he explains that his faith did not begin as certainty.
When Brann was a child, he watched his sister murdered by a gang.
He spent years deciding what that event would be allowed to make him.
He chose a life built around healing, burial, protection, and service because he refused to let the people who killed her dictate the shape of his soul.
That choice, repeated for decades, is part of why Tyren has so little to grab.
Brann does not describe himself as magically immune. He simply knows the pressure feels like something trying to tell him who he is, and that question was settled a long time ago.

entries.name: 5. Necromantic Focus
entries: The final chamber contains 3 cracked funerary anchors feeding the undead focus.

{@b Disabling an anchor.} A character adjacent to an anchor can use an action and succeed on a {@dc 15} Religion or Arcana check, deal at least 15 radiant damage to it, or physically destroy it (AC 15, 15 HP, immune to poison and psychic). An obviously appropriate rite/tool solution can work without a roll.

{@b Focus pulse.} At initiative count 20, if at least one anchor remains, one marked 10-foot area erupts with necrotic energy. Creatures there make a {@dc 15} Constitution save, taking 2d6 necrotic damage on a failure or half on a success. Each disabled anchor removes one possible pulse zone; with all three disabled, the focus stops pulsing.
{@b Encounter.} 1 Wraith + 2 Wights. The party can defeat them normally or weaken the battlefield by disabling anchors while fighting.
Destroying or properly ending all three anchors permanently stops the independent undead outbreak.

entries.name: Resting and World Movement
entries: Brann can consecrate the Memorial Walk as a safe staging area after the first attack. The party can take a Short Rest there.

During that hour, any undead not yet encountered move closer to the Necromantic Focus rather than waiting in their original rooms. This can concentrate the remaining danger but does not create new undead.
If the party leaves the cemetery entirely before ending the focus, Brann keeps civilians away and closes the grounds; the undead problem continues but does not reset.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Bellweather holds public funerals and reburials after the crisis.
Brann’s standing rises because he helped ordinary people through a genuine civic emergency without demanding more authority for himself.
That contrast matters when Perrin later argues that power should concentrate in the hands of whoever can use it effectively.
After the focus is ended, the cemetery closes briefly for reburial/repairs and then returns to normal civic use. It does not become another Tyren-linked garrison or recurring dungeon.

entries.name: Milestone
entries: Remain {@b level 8}; Valen Cemetery is an independent crisis and can be played before Maren Isle or held for later.

data.name: Chapter 14: Maren Isle

entries.name: Maps
