entries.name: Modern Running Sheet

rows: Resolve another independent magical crisis while giving the party practical defenses against Tyren and revealing that Tyren is physically a dragon.
Stop the river contamination, reach the island laboratory, recover the missing Varen containment research.
Approach by water or air, negotiate with the island arcanist, sabotage systems, fight guardians, or solve the contamination mechanically.
The missing containment volume and defensive research survive even if the arcanist flees or dies.
Tyren is an ancient emerald dragon; the Radiant Cage is an Imprisonment-like physical/soul binding; Ring of Mind Shielding blocks Tyren’s contact.

entries: {@i Use the existing Maren Isle map and pyramid/island structure.}

{@b Finite hostile/guardian roster:} 2 {@creature Water Weird|XMM|Water Weirds}, 2 Gargoyles, 2 {@creature Helmed Horror|XMM|Helmed Horrors}, and the arcanist using a {@creature Mage|XMM} stat block only if combat occurs.
{@b River approach:} 2 Water Weirds if the party crosses the contaminated intake channel; air/alternate approaches can bypass them.
{@b Landing defenses:} 2 Gargoyles.
{@b Pollution system:} 2 Helmed Horrors.
{@b Laboratory:} arcanist alone unless surviving guardians reach the room; the arcanist prefers bargaining/repair to dying for the experiment.

entries.name: Rewards and Treasure
entries: The fixed major reward is 1 {@item Ring of Mind Shielding|XDMG}.
The laboratory also contains 2 {@item Potion of Greater Healing|XDMG|Potions of Greater Healing} and {@b 600 gp} in saleable arcane reagents/components after contaminated materials are excluded.
The Varen containment volume is story evidence, not saleable treasure.

entries.name: Independent Crisis, Connected Research
entries: The Storen River is being poisoned by arcane experiments on Maren Isle.
The experimenter is {@b not working for Tyren}.

The arcanist acquired stolen historical material because research into psychic projection and the Radiant Well was useful to unrelated experiments. The contamination is the consequence of reckless magical engineering, not another Tyren plot.

entries.name: Portraying the Arcanist
entries: Keep the arcanist memorable without making them another campaign principal. They are brilliant, sleep-deprived, defensive about the work, and genuinely offended by the suggestion that "reckless" and "unsuccessful" mean the same thing. Their working robes were once expensive but now show singed hems, ink stains, hurried repairs, and pockets full of tools. Protective lenses are usually pushed up onto the forehead until something begins sparking.

The arcanist talks quickly when discussing mechanisms and much more slowly when forced to discuss consequences. They have spent so long treating danger as a solvable technical problem that they initially describe poisoned water and psychic intrusion with the same detached vocabulary.
They are {@b not working for Tyren}. Their worst decisions came from curiosity, ego, and the belief that understanding a dangerous thing is the same as controlling it.

When the party proves the experiment is hurting people, the arcanist may respond with denial, repair, surrender, bargaining, or escalation. Give them room to choose denial, repair, surrender, bargaining, or doubling down according to how the characters approach them.
This separation is important.

entries.name: 1. Following the River
entries: Residents, healers, boat crews, and travelers agree on the basic facts:

items: contamination begins near the island;
ordinary purification is unreliable;
strange lights appear over the pyramid;
altered aquatic predators gather near discharge points.

entries: If the party crosses the contaminated intake channel by water, use exactly 2 {@creature Water Weird|XMM|Water Weirds}. Air travel, a different landing, or an equally sound route can bypass them without replacement combat.

entries.name: 2. Island Defenses
entries: The island has a finite defensive system rather than a monster menu.
{@b Landing:} 2 Gargoyles animate when an unauthorized creature reaches the primary landing/pyramid approach.
{@b Pollution room:} 2 Helmed Horrors defend the pumping controls and follow the arcanist's last standing order.
If the landing alarm sounds, the arcanist secures the Varen volume and orders the Helmed Horrors to guard the pollution controls. No extra guardians appear.
The party can negotiate once it reaches the arcanist; destroying the laboratory is never required.

entries.name: 3. The Pollution System
entries: The contamination comes from three linked failures. All three must be shut down or stabilized.

{@b Feed Valve A — jammed wheel.} A character can spend an action and succeed on a {@dc 15} Strength (Athletics) check to force it closed. Appropriate leverage/tools used with time close it automatically.

{@b Feed Valve B — arcane conduit.} A character can spend an action and succeed on a {@dc 15} Arcana check, cast {@spell Dispel Magic}, or physically break the exposed conduit (AC 16, 20 HP, immune to poison and psychic).

{@b Reservoir C — cracked support.} A character can stabilize it with an action and a {@dc 15} Investigation check using appropriate tools/materials, or spend two actions bracing it manually with available workshop equipment. An obviously effective spell can solve it directly.

{@b System pulse.} At initiative count 20 while any two or more failures remain active, one marked line/zone vents contaminated force. Creatures there make a {@dc 15} Dexterity save, taking 2d6 acid or poison damage (choose whichever matches the map description) on a failure or half on a success.
{@b Encounter.} 2 Helmed Horrors defend the controls. The party can shut down systems while fighting.
Once all three failures are resolved, no further pollution enters the river; existing contamination clears over the following days.

entries.name: The Arcanist’s Starting State
entries: The arcanist wants to save the experiment, preserve the research, and avoid being dragged back to Bellweather in chains. The arcanist does not want civilians poisoned and initially minimizes how severe the contamination is.

The arcanist knows the pumping system, the stolen Varen text, the Ring of Mind Shielding research, and that something contacted the laboratory telepathically. The arcanist does not know Perrin's bargain or Tyren's political network.

If the party demonstrates the contamination clearly or shuts down part of the system without destroying the research, the arcanist will bargain and help finish the shutdown. If attacked first, use the Mage stat block and have the arcanist surrender or flee once the guardians are gone and defeat is obvious.

entries.name: 4. Psychic Research Room
entries: The arcanist has been experimenting with defenses against telepathic intrusion because the stolen Varen text described unwanted psychic contact.
This room gives the party concrete rules knowledge.

entries.name: Ring of Mind Shielding
entries: One {@item Ring of Mind Shielding} is present as a research tool or secured item.

For this campaign, a creature wearing the ring is {@b immune to Tyren’s influence and control} because Tyren must establish unwanted telepathic contact before any of his supernatural control effects can function.
This is a Tyren-specific interaction. All other rules for the item remain unchanged.

entries.name: Other Defenses
entries: Research establishes several ways to help against Tyren:

items: effects that prevent or end the {@b Charmed} condition interfere with his ordinary influence;
{@i Protection from Evil and Good} does not automatically work simply because Tyren is a dragon, but wards specifically designed against telepathic contact do;
{@i Greater Restoration} can remove lingering psychic residue or a long-running control affliction after the connection is broken;
{@spell mind blank} represents the kind of total protection Tyren cannot penetrate.

entries: The PCs’ anchored-mind resistance remains special and is not replaced by these tools.

entries.name: 5. The Missing Varen Volume
entries: The stolen Marren volume is here.
Its surviving text finally identifies the being beneath Varen Keep:
{@b TYREN — ANCIENT EMERALD DRAGON. SUBJECT’S PHYSICAL FORM REMAINS LIVING. PSYCHIC DISPERSAL MUST BE RECALLED BEFORE CONTAINMENT.}
A later passage describes the Radiant Cage as a unique ritual combining effects recognizable as {@i Imprisonment} and soul-binding magic.
The book confirms:

items: Tyren’s body is beneath Varen Keep;
the Radiant Well powers the Cage;
the Unturned were required because ordinary ritual participants could not remain themselves near Tyren;
breaking the Cage without first dealing with Tyren’s external network could release an ancient dragon with immediate access to dominated minds outside the prison.

entries: This is the dragon reveal.

entries.name: 6. Why Tyren Has Not Simply Escaped
entries: The research answers an important rules question.
Tyren can project thought through willing or compromised minds, but the Cage still binds {@b his body, soul, and permanent identity} to the lower chamber.
He can possess or dominate people temporarily.
He cannot permanently transfer himself into a new host while the Cage holds.
Perrin’s bargain did not release Tyren. It created a legal-sized crack in a prison designed to stop force.

entries.name: Resting, Alarm, and Site Aftermath
entries: A Short Rest before the pollution system is shut down gives the arcanist an hour to secure portable research, move the Varen volume into a locked laboratory cabinet, and fully alert the Helmed Horrors. The contamination also continues for that hour.
A Short Rest after the pollution system is shut down is safe if the arcanist has surrendered, agreed to cooperate, fled, or been defeated.

Afterward, Bellweather's healers/surveyors monitor the river and the island laboratory is either placed under supervision, abandoned, or left to a cooperating arcanist according to the party's outcome. The crisis does not require the party to occupy the island.

entries.name: The Arcanist’s Fate
entries: The arcanist can surrender, bargain, flee, or fight depending on the party’s approach.
The arcanist remains a one-chapter NPC unless the players choose to maintain the relationship.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: The river begins clearing.
The party now knows the threat is not an abstract spirit.
There is an {@b ancient emerald dragon alive beneath Varen Keep}.
The next question is how far his network has already spread.

entries.name: Milestone
entries: Advance to {@b level 9} after Maren Isle and the dragon truth are resolved.

data.name: Chapter 15: The Lands Beyond Bellweather
entries: {@b Recommended level:} 9–14 {@b Expected milestones:} 10–14 across the arc {@b Likely table time:} about 5–8 sessions depending on player choices

rows: Show Tyren attempting to scale beyond Bellweather, let the party choose regional allies and evidence, and bring the Perrin bargain into the open.
Trace the network outside the city, protect independent communities, break at least one external control route, gather enough evidence to confront Perrin.
The party chooses which regional locations matter. No requirement to “clear the map.”
Losing one alliance strengthens later complications but does not block the campaign.
Bellweather is the prototype, Perrin is Tyren’s willing conduit, and Tyren’s goal extends far beyond the city.

entries: {@b This is a choice-driven arc, not a checklist.} The party can visit regional locations in any order and can leave some unused.
{@b Level scaling for regional combat.} When a location has an optional hostile force, use the exact row for the party's current level band rather than inventing a new roster.
{@b Long rests.} Allied settlements are safe once trust is earned. During active pursuits, raids, or relay operations, time continues to move.
{@b Core proof is redundant.} No single settlement, courier, elder, or resonator is required to prove Tyren's expansion.

entries.name: Regional Combat Scaling
entries: Use a location-specific roster when listed. Settlement populations never enter initiative as one group.

entries.name: Regional Rewards
entries: Use the listed reward for each regional module. There is no automatic permanent magic-item payout for this arc.
Kerren: 1 Potion of Greater Healing plus route maps/safe passage.
Waylen: guides, mounts, trade relationship, and one automatic hostile-road bypass.
Rellan: the ritual charm that grants one automatic Chorus Chamber success.
Emmer: 500 gp in trade credit/materials plus 1 Potion of Superior Healing.
Tyren's Regional Countermove: recovered operating funds worth 500 gp plus 1 Potion of Superior Healing if the party secures the hostile team's supplies.
Unused regional locations grant nothing automatically; rewards come from what the party actually does.

entries.name: Regional Rule
entries: Every named regional place remains part of the campaign world, but the party does not need to complete all of them.
Milestones come from changing Tyren's position: proving the spread, breaking routes, gaining allies, confronting Perrin, surviving the response, and completing endgame preparation.
A location solved earlier can still matter later if the party uses that alliance or evidence in a new way. Do not force unused locations just to award a level.
The four named locations below each serve a distinct function and are ready to run as one-session regional modules.

entries.name: Kerren Settlement
entries: Kerren is a thri-kreen settlement built among earthen mounds and underground chambers. It is a community, not a dungeon.

entries.name: Why It Matters
entries: Kerren sits on a courier route whose travelers now stop, turn, and depart in synchronized patterns without visible messages.

entries.name: Table-Ready Kerren Module
entries: {@b Route roster:} 1 Veteran and 4 Scouts operate the outside courier/recovery route. Kerren residents are not part of this hostile roster.

Respectful contact, useful trade, translation magic, or help with a local practical problem earns a meeting without a check. If the party demands immediate access or arrives during tension, a {@dc 15} Persuasion or Insight check can accelerate cooperation; failure costs time rather than permanently closing Kerren.

{@b Observation.} Three courier pairs pass the route during a 90-minute cycle. Watching the full cycle automatically reveals identical stops and timing. A {@dc 15} Investigation or Survival check identifies the pattern after 20 minutes.

{@b Interception.} If the party stops a courier pair, use 2 Scouts. If the pair fails to report, the Veteran and remaining 2 Scouts arrive about 20 minutes later to recover them. They withdraw if the Veteran falls or the prisoners/documents are clearly lost.
A captured courier remembers an instruction becoming 'obvious' without hearing a voice. Route marks ultimately connect back to Bellweather commerce.

entries.name: Reward
entries: Kerren provides route maps, safe passage, supplies, and 1 {@item Potion of Greater Healing|XDMG}. The alliance can remove one travel complication later.

entries.name: Waylen Camp
entries: Waylen Camp is a mobile mixed-species community of herders, hunters, guides, and traders.

entries.name: Why It Matters
entries: Waylen has watched entire merchant and troop columns stop, turn, and change camp without visible messengers. Its guides can show that the synchronized routes point back toward Bellweather.

entries.name: Table-Ready Waylen Module
entries: The camp asks for one concrete favor before committing guides: escort a supply caravan through a road where ordinary raiders have been attacking. The raiders are unrelated to Tyren.
{@b Raider roster:} 1 Veteran + 4 Scouts. They try to take animals/cargo and disengage once half the group is defeated or the caravan reaches the marked safe bend.

{@b Caravan objective:} use 3 wagon/animal groups. At initiative count 20, one unprotected group moves or scatters 15 feet toward danger. A character adjacent to it can use an action to stabilize or guide it automatically.

After the escort, Waylen guides share months of observations. Comparing the route notes makes the Bellweather-origin pattern automatic; no investigation roll is required once the records are placed together.

entries.name: Reward
entries: Waylen provides guides, mounts, a standing trade relationship, and a route that lets the party bypass one later hostile-road encounter entirely.

entries.name: Rellan Enclave
entries: Rellan is a lizardfolk enclave built around flooded ruins and old stonework. It is a community, not a monster lair.

entries.name: Why It Matters
entries: Rellan oral tradition remembers a green-glass dragon whose voice moved through other mouths and a few people who could stand before it without bowing.

entries.name: Table-Ready Rellan Module
entries: The enclave does not demand violence as a price for lore. The party can earn access by respectful diplomacy or by helping reopen a flooded ancestral shrine.
{@b Flooded shrine roster:} 1 {@creature Giant Crocodile|XMM} and 2 {@creature Giant Constrictor Snake|XMM|Giant Constrictor Snakes}. They are wild animals, not Tyren servants.

{@b Shrine objective:} three stone drains are jammed. Clearing a drain takes an action and a {@dc 15} Athletics check, appropriate tools, or two uninterrupted actions of manual clearing. Once all three are open, the water falls and the animals can retreat rather than fight to the death.
If the party refuses the shrine job, a patient diplomatic approach can still earn the lore after a day of discussion or trade. The lore is not gated behind combat.

entries.name: The Missing Ritual Detail
entries: Rellan tradition supplies the missing principle: the old ritual pulled dispersed thought back toward Tyren's permanent identity before sealing body, soul, and name together.
That is the conceptual key to understanding why reversing the Radiant Well is dangerous.

entries.name: Reward
entries: Rellan provides safe passage and a prepared ritual charm. During Chapter 17, using it at the Chorus Chamber automatically counts as one successful node action.

entries.name: Emmer Hold
entries: Emmer Hold is a fortified kobold-majority mining and engineering community. Most residents want trade and survival, not war. A militant faction has become unnaturally synchronized.

entries.name: Why It Matters
entries: This is Tyren's clearest attempt to maintain a controlled group outside Bellweather.

entries.name: Militant Roster by Party Level
entries: Four additional kobold engineers are present around the command area but are frightened noncombatants unless the party attacks them.

entries.name: The Psychic Relay
entries: The emerald resonator is held by three control rods.
A character adjacent to a rod can disable it with an action and a {@dc 15} Arcana check, appropriate engineering/thieves' tools, or physical destruction (AC 16, 15 HP, immune to poison and psychic).
When the third rod is disabled, the resonator shuts down. Controlled militants lose the unnatural coordination and surviving members individually choose whether to surrender, flee, or keep fighting.
At initiative count 20 while the relay is active, one militant who can see another can move up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks as Tyren synchronizes the group.

entries.name: Adventure Approaches
entries: The party can expose the militant leadership, infiltrate the command chamber, destroy the resonator, negotiate with worried families, or fight while protecting noncombatants. Reaching the relay is the real objective; exterminating the hold is never required.

entries.name: Evidence
entries: The relay's shipping container came through the same commercial intermediary network seen at Koven House. Combined with the outward-spread pattern, this materially strengthens the case against Perrin's network even though the container carries no confession.

entries.name: Reward
entries: If the hold is freed rather than conquered, Bellweather gains skilled engineers, a safer trade route, {@b 500 gp} in trade credit/materials, and 1 {@item Potion of Superior Healing|XDMG}.

entries.name: Regional Milestones

rows: First major regional success proves synchronized control is spreading outward from Bellweather
Party materially breaks an external route/relay and secures a meaningful ally or safe route
Party confronts Perrin with the accumulated case and his bargain becomes explicit
Party survives/stops Tyren's regional countermove after the confrontation
Party converts regional gains into a viable endgame plan against Bellweather's central network

entries: These are story changes, not location checkboxes. An especially strong player-created success can satisfy the same milestone.

entries.name: When to Confront Perrin
entries: The party has enough to confront Perrin once it has reached level 11 and can establish both: Tyren's influence is spreading beyond Bellweather, and the external network still traces back through Bellweather routes or financing.
The confrontation can happen in Bellweather, at Ledger House, before the Council, or somewhere the party chooses. Do not force a special confrontation room.

No single Persuasion roll determines Perrin's state. Judge Cracked, Defiant, or Hostile from the evidence presented, prior relationship, and choices. Use a {@dc 16} social check only when a specific uncertain argument genuinely turns on delivery rather than facts.

entries.name: Confronting Perrin
entries: The case can be built from several independent pieces of evidence; no single perfect proof is required.
By now the party can reasonably assemble several independent facts:

items: Koven House financing touched Cardon-connected intermediaries;
Perrin benefited politically from criminal coordination;
Tyren requires a willing conduit to reach beyond the Radiant Cage;
synchronized expansion originates in Bellweather;
Perrin has repeatedly been near critical moments of unnatural obedience;
Perrin’s rise has coincided with the growth of the network.

entries: If the players reach a different theory first, let them investigate it. NPC exposition does not force suspicion of Perrin.
When they finally confront Perrin directly with Tyren, the Spirit, or the unexplained influence, Perrin has reached a point where he no longer wants to pretend the power itself is shameful.

entries.name: Perrin Tells the Truth
entries: Perrin admits that a presence beneath Bellweather came to him before the campaign.
He believed it was the Spirit of the City.
It knew the city. It knew the Cardon family. It offered him the power he needed to restore both.
He admits using that power to influence people.
He admits organizing the criminal coalition to discredit the Council.
He admits that the Spirit began using the network in ways he did not order.
He does {@b not} describe himself as Tyren’s servant.
He believes he has been using a dangerous power for Bellweather’s benefit.

entries.name: The Party’s Strongest Argument
entries: The party can tell Perrin that Tyren is an ancient emerald dragon imprisoned for trying to control the city fifty years ago.
Perrin does not have to deny the records anymore.
His answer should reveal how far he has moved:
{@b “Then the old city was afraid of the same thing you’re afraid of now: a power that works.”}
The exact wording can vary; preserve the underlying idea.
Perrin now believes the moral question is not whether control is wrong in the abstract. He believes the question is {@b who uses it and for what purpose}.

entries.name: Can the Party Turn Perrin Here?
entries: They can shake him.
They can make him doubt Tyren.
They can affect how he behaves later.
A single Persuasion check cannot erase years of choices or end the campaign.
Likewise, Perrin remains persuadable in principle; meaningful change requires accumulated evidence, relationship, and choices.
Record the quality of the confrontation:
{@b Cracked:} Perrin is visibly shaken and begins secretly considering a way out.
{@b Defiant:} Perrin believes the party is too frightened of power to understand what Bellweather needs.
{@b Hostile:} Perrin concludes the party will destroy everything he has built if he does not stop them.
This state affects Chapter 17.

entries.name: Perrin’s Core Refusal
entries: Whatever his emotional state, Perrin does {@b not} surrender the power voluntarily here.
He believes giving it up would abandon Bellweather to the same indecision and weakness he has spent years overcoming.
The corruption arc is now explicit.

entries.name: Tyren’s Regional Countermove
entries: After Perrin is confronted and the party reaches level 12, Tyren attempts to preserve the outward network by striking one regional ally or route the party already cares about. Choose the location whose loss would matter most based on actual play.

{@b Countermove roster:} 1 Gladiator, 2 Veterans, 1 Mage, and 4 Scouts. Their objective is to install or recover an emerald resonator, destroy route records, or seize a key witness—not to fight to the last person.

{@b Resonator objective:} use the same three-control-rod mechanics as Emmer Hold (DC 15 or AC 16/15 HP per rod). If the party prevents installation, destroys the device, or evacuates the threatened people/evidence, the countermove fails.

If the party already eliminated every plausible regional node, convert the countermove into an attempted seizure of one allied caravan or delegation traveling toward Bellweather rather than inventing a new faction.
Stopping the countermove advances the party to {@b level 13}.

entries.name: Regional Rest, Travel, and World Movement
entries: Once trusted, Kerren, Waylen, Rellan, and a freed Emmer can each support a safe Long Rest.

If the party pauses for a Short or Long Rest during an active chase, raid, relay shutdown, or countermove, the opposing objective advances normally: couriers travel, raiders move cargo, militants fortify the relay, or witnesses relocate.
Do not create random punishment encounters merely because the party rests. Apply consequences tied to the active situation.

entries.name: Completing the Regional Arc
entries: After Tyren's countermove, the party chooses how to turn earlier regional successes into endgame preparation. One additional meaningful operation is enough: destroy a remaining relay, secure the Rellan ritual, formalize a Kerren or Waylen route, free Emmer, or execute an equivalent player-created plan.

If all of those were already achieved before the confrontation, the party can instead coordinate two existing allies to sever a major route into Bellweather. Do not force unused locations solely for leveling.

entries.name: Milestone
entries: Advance the party to {@b level 14} when its regional allies, routes, and evidence form a credible plan to act against Bellweather's central network.
Unused locations remain in the world and may still matter later.

data.name: Chapter 16: Zennar Outpost
entries: {@b Recommended level:} 14 {@b Expected milestone:} 15 {@b Likely table time:} 1–2 sessions

rows: Make Perrin’s corruption undeniable: he uses civic authority to remove the people threatening his control.
Detect the betrayal, survive or overturn the trap, preserve evidence, return to Bellweather.
Inspect the packet, approach covertly, negotiate with the outpost, fake compliance, escape, expose the order, or fight a limited strike force.
Evidence exists in multiple forms. Capture becomes an escape/social sequence, not campaign-ending helplessness.
Perrin is now using institutions and coercive power to protect his own position, not merely Bellweather.

entries: {@b Finite outpost roster relevant to the plot:} 1 Knight commandant, 1 Spy covert handler, 1 Assassin, 2 Veterans, 1 Mage, and 8 Guards. Other soldiers remain background personnel unless the party deliberately starts a battle with the whole outpost.
{@b Default strike force:} Assassin + 2 Veterans + Mage + 4 Guards.
{@b Reserve/non-hostile personnel:} commandant + Spy + 4 Guards. Their allegiance depends on what the party proves and how the order is handled.
{@b Victory target:} evidence plus freedom to return to Bellweather. Clearing the outpost is not required.

entries.name: Rewards and Treasure
entries: If the commandant rejects Perrin's order or later accepts that the party was wrongfully targeted, the outpost provides {@b 1,000 gp total} in restitution/supplies and 2 {@item Potion of Superior Healing|XDMG|Potions of Superior Healing}.
The hidden order, commandant copy, witnesses, and courier record are the campaign-critical rewards.

rows: Commandant party, only if negotiations collapse

entries.name: Why Perrin Sends Them
entries: By level 14 the party has:

items: identified Tyren as an ancient emerald dragon;
learned the Radiant Cage exists;
confronted Perrin about the bargain;
damaged Tyren’s regional expansion;
become the people most capable of exposing Perrin and stopping the Well from being reversed.

entries: Perrin now believes the party threatens everything he has built.
Tyren does not need to dominate Perrin into betraying them.
Perrin makes the choice.

entries.name: The Official Mission
entries: Perrin presents an urgent diplomatic/security assignment to {@b Zennar Outpost}.
The visible mission is plausible: establish whether the outpost will cooperate against regional instability and whether it can help isolate Varen Keep.
The party receives sealed credentials and instructions.
The packet contains a second order for the Zennar commandant.

entries.name: Perrin’s Betrayal by State
entries: Use the Perrin state recorded after the party confronted him.

{@b Cracked Perrin:} the hidden order demands detention, disarmament, and removal from Bellweather’s affairs. It authorizes lethal force if the party resists. Perrin tells himself he is preventing a civil conflict, not ordering murder.
{@b Defiant Perrin:} the order describes the party as compromised by Tyren research and authorizes permanent removal if capture is impractical.
{@b Hostile Perrin:} the order is explicitly lethal and asks for proof of death.
All three versions are betrayals.
Cracked Perrin remains responsible even when his wording is softer.

entries.name: 1. The Road to Zennar
entries: Give the party one quiet opportunity to inspect the sealed packet before arrival.

Opening and resealing it with appropriate magic succeeds automatically if the method logically leaves no trace. Careful mundane opening uses a {@dc 15} Dexterity check with thieves' tools, forgery kit, or another appropriate tool. Failure still reveals the hidden order but leaves obvious evidence of tampering.
If the party refuses to tamper with official papers, later warning signs expose the trap. Reading the order early is an advantage, not a gate.

entries.name: 2. Approach
entries: Zennar is a disciplined frontier outpost, not a dungeon full of enemies waiting for initiative.
A patrol escorts diplomatic visitors to a controlled reception area.
The soldiers are professional and do not all know about the hidden order.

entries.name: 3. Warning Signs
entries: If the party has not opened the packet, give redundant clues:

items: quarters chosen for containment rather than comfort;
unusual interest in where the party stores weapons;
civilians moved out of their corridor;
a second courier arriving from Bellweather with updated instructions;
guards who appear confused about whether the party is guest or prisoner.

entries: Successful Insight or Investigation reveals the danger earlier. Failure never erases it.

After the party notices any two warning signs, a {@dc 15} Insight or Investigation check confirms that the outpost is preparing containment rather than hospitality. Failure delays certainty until the commandant meeting; it does not preserve the surprise indefinitely.

entries.name: 4. The Commandant’s Choice
entries: The commandant is not part of the recurring cast. Use a {@creature Knight|XMM} or {@creature Veteran|XMM} as needed.
The commandant may dislike Perrin’s instruction but still consider it legally valid.
The party can:

items: expose contradictions in the order;
present evidence of Tyren;
convince the commandant Perrin is compromised;
steal the outpost’s copy;
bargain for release;
fake compliance;
escape.

entries: A strong social solution should be as valid as combat.

If the party presents two credible contradictions or two forms of Tyren/Perrin evidence, the commandant pauses enforcement automatically long enough to investigate. Use a {@dc 15} Persuasion check only when the evidence is ambiguous and the party is asking the commandant to take a personal or legal risk beyond what the facts already justify.

entries.name: 5. Assassination or Arrest Attempt
entries: If the betrayal reaches violence, use the fixed strike force: 1 Assassin, 2 Veterans, 1 Mage, and 4 Guards.

{@b Starting positions.} The Veterans and 2 Guards control the nearest exit; the Mage begins behind cover; 2 Guards hold the secondary corridor; the Assassin begins concealed only if the party failed to identify the trap before the meeting.
The strike force's objective depends on Perrin's state: Cracked seeks disarmament/detention first; Defiant accepts lethal force when resistance becomes serious; Hostile begins with lethal intent.

Attackers withdraw or surrender when the commandant publicly rescinds the order, the Mage or Assassin is defeated and the operation becomes untenable, or evidence makes the action publicly indefensible.
Do not add the remaining outpost garrison to initiative unless the party deliberately attacks uninvolved soldiers.

entries.name: If the Party Submits to Detention
entries: Detention is an active social/escape sequence, not a campaign-ending cutscene.

The party is placed in two adjacent secured rooms. Obvious weapons are stored in a locked armory room across the corridor; worn armor, clothing, holy symbols, and non-obvious personal items remain unless the party gave the outpost a specific reason to search more aggressively.
Exactly 4 Guards rotate on the detention corridor. The commandant reviews the order within an hour, creating time for persuasion, message-sending, tool or magic use, or escape.
If the party proves the order compromised before escaping, the commandant releases them. If they escape first, the same documentary evidence can later clear the legal ambiguity.

entries.name: Resting and Time
entries: Before the betrayal is exposed, the party can rest as diplomatic guests, but the outpost continues processing Perrin's order.
A Short Rest after warning signs gives the covert handler time to position the fixed strike force and move the party's assigned quarters into containment posture.
Once the commandant has suspended or rescinded the order, or the party has escaped the outpost, normal resting becomes possible. No new strike team appears.

entries.name: 6. Evidence
entries: The party can secure up to four forms of proof:

items: the original hidden order;
the commandant’s received copy;
testimony from personnel who were briefed on the operation;
a Bellweather courier record showing the order originated through Perrin’s office.

entries: Two credible forms are enough to make denial politically difficult.

entries.name: Return to Bellweather
entries: The city they return to should feel {@b better and worse at the same time}.
Crime is down.
Major streets are orderly.
Construction and trade are moving quickly.
Public disputes end unusually fast.
People praise Perrin for stabilizing the city while the party was away.
And something is wrong.

Groups of citizens repeat the same phrases. Workers change plans simultaneously. Clerks approve requests they had rejected minutes earlier. People who later come out of the effect cannot explain why a decision felt so obviously correct.
Bellweather is becoming Tyren’s successful prototype.
If the commandant sided with the party, a sealed copy of the outpost record travels separately toward Bellweather so Perrin cannot erase the entire incident by intercepting the PCs.

entries.name: Default Council Positions on Return
entries: Adjust these according to actual play, but use them as a baseline if nothing else has changed.

{@b Wern Ursen} has been removed from direct command or politically sidelined after refusing to place the entire guard structure under Perrin’s unified emergency authority. Perrin uses Wern’s genuinely harsh earlier policies to make the removal look reasonable.

{@b Ulric Evern} remains institutionally active but has unexplained gaps in memory and has signed several decrees he does not remember drafting. Tyren can control Ulric because Ulric is not anchored like Brann or Brakkus. Ulric becomes powerful evidence that something supernatural is happening inside government.

{@b Bishop Brann} publicly refuses to endorse permanent emergency control. He cannot be mentally seized, so Perrin has to isolate, discredit, or politically work around him rather than simply switch him off.

{@creature Brakkus Ledgerhelm|NCFASOC} keeps Ledger House functioning as a refuge. He is not leading an armed rebellion. He simply refuses to hand guests over without lawful cause and cannot be compelled to change his mind supernaturally.

entries.name: No Cause for Alarm Beat
entries: Notices appear throughout Bellweather:

{@b CIVIC NOTICE:} Bellweather remains secure. Essential services are operating at record capacity. Reports of widespread coercion and administrative irregularity are being investigated. Residents are asked to avoid rumor and disruption. {@b There is no cause for alarm.}
At this point the phrase should be frightening precisely because much of the city really does look calm.

entries.name: Perrin’s Point of No Return
entries: The Zennar order matters because Perrin is no longer using control only to solve civic problems.
He used the city’s institutions to protect {@b his own power} from people who could expose him.
Whatever good he still wants for Bellweather, the distinction between the city’s needs and Perrin’s needs has collapsed.

entries.name: Preparing for Varen
entries: The party can return openly, gather Brann/Brakkus/Ulric/Wern as allies, use regional contacts, or move covertly.
Allies should reduce complications rather than join the dragon fight as DM-controlled heroes.
Examples:

items: Brakkus keeps controlled civilians and guards from overwhelming the party’s escape route;
Brann protects noncombatants and helps break a citywide influence pulse;
Wern provides routes, timing, and military intelligence;
Ulric exposes legal orders and removes bureaucratic barriers;
regional allies cut off reinforcements or supply routes.

entries.name: Milestone
entries: Advance to {@b level 15} when the Zennar betrayal is survived and credible evidence of Perrin's order is preserved.
Level 16 comes after the party materially breaks or bypasses controlled Bellweather's network and opens a viable route to Varen Keep.

data.name: Chapter 17: Varen Keep and the Radiant Cage

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/varen_keep.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/varen_keep.webp}
{@b Recommended level:} 15–16 {@b Campaign finale} {@b Likely table time:} 3–5 sessions including the controlled-Bellweather return

entries.name: Modern Running Sheet

rows: Stop Tyren’s attempt to reverse the Radiant Cage, confront Perrin’s choices, release and defeat the dragon, and decide Bellweather’s political and magical future.
Reach the lower keep, disable the outward-control network, stop the Well reversal, survive Tyren’s release, defeat the ancient emerald dragon.
Infiltration, coalition assault, secret routes, sabotage, negotiation with controlled defenders, or direct attack. Perrin’s final stance depends on earlier play.
Missing objectives makes the dragon fight harder; it never removes the dragon payoff or ends the campaign through one failed check.
The “Spirit of the City” is physically real, physically imprisoned, and has used Perrin as the door through which an old conquest could begin again.

entries: {@i Use the existing Varen Keep map. Run it as set pieces rather than a room-by-room clear.}

entries.name: Return to Controlled Bellweather
entries: The party returns from Zennar at {@b level 15}. Bellweather is safer, cleaner, busier, and more efficient—and visibly less voluntary.
Crime is sharply reduced. Work crews move on schedule. Public projects advance. Residents repeat the same reassuring phrases and sometimes obey minor instructions before realizing they were given.
Brakkus and Bishop Brann remain fully themselves. Jord and the PCs can feel Tyren's pressure but remain subject only to the established one-action Command ceiling.

This is not a street-by-street reclamation chapter. The party needs to accomplish {@b any two} of the four approaches below, or an equivalent player-created plan, to materially break or bypass the city network and open a credible route to Varen Keep.
If Tyren directly presses an anchored PC during the controlled-city phase, use a {@dc 16} Wisdom save and the established one-turn Command ceiling. A Ring of Mind Shielding grants immunity.

entries.name: Breaking Controlled Bellweather
Approach A — Public Proof
entries: Use the Zennar order plus Council/archive records to make Perrin's betrayal publicly undeniable.

Ulric can authenticate civic records if reached. If Tyren is actively controlling him, severing him from the immediate relay with {@spell Greater Restoration}, a {@item Ring of Mind Shielding|XDMG}, or destruction of the nearby signal crystal lets him testify normally.
If controlled security intervenes, use 1 Knight + 2 Veterans + 1 Mage. Their job is to seize records and remove witnesses, not attack crowds.
Two credible documentary sources plus one living institutional witness are enough; no Persuasion roll is required once the proof is public.

entries.name: Approach B — Break Guard Synchronization
entries: Wern can identify the guard signal relay coordinating patrol changes.
Use 1 Mage + 2 Veterans + 4 Guards at the relay.

The relay has three exposed signal crystals (AC 16, 15 HP each, immune to poison and psychic). A character can instead disable a crystal with an action and a {@dc 16} Arcana or appropriate-tools check.
When all three are disabled, controlled guard units stop moving as one body; individual guards must decide what to do.

entries.name: Approach C — Hold the Refuge
entries: Perrin's administration attempts to place Ledger House and Brann's refuge network under emergency control.
Use 1 Knight + 2 Veterans + 4 Guards. Brakkus and Brann protect civilians and refuse unlawful transfer; they do not replace the PCs in combat.
The party succeeds by keeping the refuge open, exposing the order, forcing the arrest detail to stand down, or removing its relay contact. Nonlethal resolution is fully valid.

entries.name: Approach D — Quiet Route
entries: Use Savin or Marren maps, regional guides, old service tunnels, or a player-created infiltration plan to bypass the civic network entirely.

Run 3 successes before 2 complications. The default DC for an uncertain Stealth, Survival, Investigation, thieves' tools, or similar action is {@dc 16}. An established route provided by an ally counts as one automatic success.
A complication costs time, closes one route, or causes a small patrol to investigate; it does not erase prior successes.

{@b Milestone to 16.} Advance the party to {@b level 16} once any two approaches, or equivalent player-created achievements, have broken or bypassed the city control network and opened a viable route to Varen Keep.
{@b Finite Varen roster before Tyren:} 2 Knights, 6 Veterans, 8 Guards, 3 Mages, and 4 Helmed Horrors, plus Perrin. No room creates additional defenders.
{@b Outer watchpost:} 1 Knight + 2 Veterans + 2 Guards.
{@b Thorn/service route:} 1 Helmed Horror.
{@b Lower barracks:} 1 Mage + 2 Veterans + 2 Guards.
{@b Chorus Chamber:} 1 Mage + 2 Veterans + 1 Helmed Horror.
{@b Civic Relay:} 1 Knight + 4 Guards.
{@b Well Reversal:} 1 Mage + 2 Helmed Horrors.
{@b Final fight:} Tyren uses the full official {@creature Ancient Emerald Dragon|FTD} stat block plus only the complications from nodes the party failed to disable.

entries.name: Rewards and Treasure
entries: Do not require a pre-fight treasure payout for balance. The party enters the finale with equipment earned during the campaign.

After Tyren, the Radiant Well, surviving Cardon property, seized criminal or civic assets, and Bellweather's settlement are story rewards. Any major permanent-item division can be handled as epilogue treasure instead of something the DM must prepare before the dragon fight.

entries.name: The Situation
entries: Tyren and Perrin are attempting to reverse the Radiant Well.

Perrin believes fully opening the Well will give him enough power to end Bellweather’s instability permanently. He now sees direct control as an efficient form of governance: crime can be stopped before it begins, corrupt officials can be made to act properly, and civic projects can proceed without obstruction.
Tyren wants something much larger.

The same reversed current that would let Perrin dominate Bellweather will let Tyren push his mind outward through every connected person, relay, trade route, and controlled node the network has established.
Bellweather is the first city.
Tyren intends it to be the first of many.

entries.name: Why the Dragon Fight Is Guaranteed
entries: The party cannot solve the campaign by simply leaving Tyren sealed while breaking a few political connections.
The Radiant Cage and outward-control network have become entangled.
To stop Tyren from broadcasting through the Well, the party must disable the mechanisms reversing the current.
Doing so forces Tyren’s dispersed psychic presence back toward his physical body—the same principle used by the Unturned fifty years ago.
But fifty years of strain, Perrin’s willing conduit, and the reversed Well have damaged the original prison beyond repair.
When the party successfully stops the outward broadcast, the {@b Radiant Cage fails physically}.
Tyren is released.
Stopping the mind-control apocalypse causes the final dragon fight.
That is the price of ending the threat instead of postponing it.

entries.name: Finale Structure
entries: Run Varen Keep as four major stages.

entries.name: Stage 1 — Reach the Lower Keep
entries: Use the existing Varen map as three set pieces rather than a room-by-room clear.

{@b Outer watchpost.} 1 Knight + 2 Veterans + 2 Guards protect an alarm crystal. A character adjacent to it can disable it with an action and a {@dc 16} Arcana or tools check or destroy it (AC 16, 20 HP). If disabled before the end of round 2, the lower barracks does not begin alerted.
{@b Thorn/service route.} 1 Helmed Horror patrols the constricted approach. A service route opened by allies can bypass this set piece entirely.
{@b Lower barracks.} 1 Mage + 2 Veterans + 2 Guards hold the descent. They are controlled or professional defenders and can be freed, bypassed, or forced to surrender.
Each major ally benefit earned before the finale may remove one entire set-piece complication. Removed defenders do not reappear elsewhere.

entries.name: Stage 2 — Break the Three Nodes
entries: The Radiant Cage complex contains three systems that Tyren and Perrin are using to reverse the original ritual.
The party can tackle them in any order.

entries.name: Node A: The Chorus Chamber
entries: This chamber maintains Tyren's active connection to controlled minds outside the Keep.
{@b Defenders:} 1 Mage + 2 Veterans + 1 Helmed Horror.
{@b Objective:} earn 3 successes before 2 complications while at least one character can interact with the resonance array.

The default DC for an uncertain Arcana, Religion, tools, or physical-control action is {@dc 16}. Using the Rellan ritual charm counts as one automatic success. A directly relevant spell or meaningful resource can count as a success without a roll when it clearly solves one part of the problem.
{@b Complication on a failed node action:} the acting character takes 3d6 psychic damage and makes a {@dc 16} Wisdom save; on a failure Tyren imposes one one-turn Command-style imperative.
{@b Benefit if disabled:} controlled reinforcements outside Varen lose coordination; Tyren cannot use Seize the Anchored; and his mind has no prepared network to flee into when the dragon body dies.

entries.name: Node B: The Civic Relay
entries: This is Perrin's administrative-magical control network: signal crystals, schedules, city maps, seals, and linked orders.
{@b Defenders:} 1 Knight + 4 Guards.
{@b Objective:} earn 3 successes before 2 complications.

Default uncertain actions use {@dc 16}. Valid approaches include destroying the central relay, replacing the command sequence with shutdown orders, using Ulric's seals, using Wern's military codes, or persuading Perrin to deactivate it.

{@b Complication on a failed node action:} one door or route locks and costs an action plus {@dc 16} Athletics, tools, or Arcana to reopen, or one Guard immediately moves up to its Speed to protect the relay.
{@b Benefit if disabled:} no controlled guard or minion support during the final fight; Bellweather begins waking before Tyren dies; Perrin loses the immediate visible proof that control works.

entries.name: Node C: The Well Reversal
entries: This mechanism is physically reversing the Radiant Well's original inward pull.
{@b Defenders:} 1 Mage + 2 Helmed Horrors.
{@b Objective:} earn 3 successes before 2 complications.
Default uncertain actions use {@dc 16}. Valid approaches include stabilizing regulators, breaking the lattice, completing part of the old Unturned rite, or forcing a shutdown.

{@b Complication on a failed node action:} a marked 15-foot zone erupts. Creatures there make a {@dc 16} Dexterity save, taking 3d6 force damage and being pushed 10 feet on a failure, or half damage with no push on a success.

{@b Benefit if disabled:} Tyren cannot project citywide during the final confrontation; the global-scale plan ends; shutting the system down starts the unavoidable physical failure of the Radiant Cage.

entries.name: Running the Nodes
entries: Each node is an objective encounter with its listed defenders. Track 3 successes before 2 complications; no single skill is required.
A failed check does not erase prior successes. It causes the listed complication and play continues.
If the party physically destroys an obvious node component and the method is clearly sufficient, treat that as a success rather than asking for a redundant skill roll.
The party can withdraw from a node and return later, but defenders at untouched nodes remain in place and Perrin continues the Well reversal.

entries.name: Resting Inside Varen Keep
entries: A Short Rest is possible in a secured area, but the reversal continues during that hour.
After the first Short Rest taken inside Varen before all three nodes are disabled, every untouched node begins fully alerted and its defenders take prepared positions.

After a second Short Rest before all three nodes are disabled, choose one untouched node; it begins with one complication already marked because Perrin and Tyren advanced the process during the delay.
Once all three nodes are disabled, a Short Rest before Tyren's release is not available: stopping the Well Reversal immediately triggers the Cage's physical failure and the final sequence.
No new defenders appear because the party rested; consequences come from preparation and the advancing mechanism.

entries.name: Stage 3 — Perrin at the Well
entries: Perrin is present in the lower complex when the final node is threatened.
This is not a mandatory boss fight against Perrin.
His behavior depends on the state recorded during the regional Perrin confrontation at level 12 and what the party has done since.

entries.name: Cracked Perrin
entries: Perrin has been trying not to admit that the party was right.
Seeing the physical containment machinery and the Well destabilizing can finally break the story he has told himself about the Spirit.
He may help disable one node, order controlled defenders to stand down, or give the party a crucial piece of access.
He still remains responsible for everything he chose before this moment.

entries.name: Defiant Perrin
entries: Perrin believes the party is about to destroy the only power capable of permanently fixing Bellweather.
He tries to stop them through guards, locks, civic authority, and the relay system.
He may still hesitate when Tyren begins speaking openly about control beyond Bellweather.

entries.name: Hostile Perrin
entries: Perrin has fused his own political survival with Bellweather’s future.
He actively attempts to keep the Well reversal running and treats the party as enemies of the city.
Use an appropriate non-boss NPC chassis if Perrin must enter combat, but keep his real power in command, access, and controlled defenders rather than suddenly turning him into a high-level wizard.

entries.name: The Truth Perrin Cannot Rationalize
entries: As the final node fails, Tyren no longer needs to maintain the fiction of being Bellweather’s benevolent spirit.
Perrin experiences the dragon’s full presence for the first time.
The party should not need a speech to understand what happened.
The chamber shakes.
Emerald light moves beneath the stone.
The enormous restraints below begin to break.
Whatever Perrin thought he made a bargain with, it has claws, wings, and a body large enough to have required a fortress to bury.
Perrin’s reaction belongs to the campaign state:

items: horror;
denial;
rage at Tyren;
desperate insistence that the party can still control the situation;
or a final attempt to help.

entries: Tyren’s deception does not erase Perrin’s agency. Perrin was deceived about what Tyren was, but Perrin knowingly chose manipulation, criminal conspiracy, direct control, and betrayal.

entries.name: The Release
entries: When the Well Reversal is stopped, the Radiant Cage performs one final version of its original purpose: it yanks Tyren’s projected consciousness back toward his own body.
The damaged prison cannot survive the return.
The lower chamber opens.
Tyren is released.
This is the campaign’s dragon payoff.

entries.name: Stage 4 — Tyren, Ancient Emerald Dragon
entries: Use the official {@creature Ancient Emerald Dragon|FTD} stat block from {@i Fizban’s Treasury of Dragons} as Tyren’s base statistics.
Use Tyren’s core ancient emerald dragon stat block at full strength. This is the final fight of a level-3-to-16 campaign and should demand major resources.
Balance the encounter through the objectives the party completed, not by quietly reducing Tyren’s identity.

entries.name: Default Final Fight
entries: If the party disabled {@b two or more nodes}, fight Tyren as the full official Ancient Emerald Dragon without an additional minion wave.
Use Varen’s lower chamber and Well as meaningful terrain.
Allow the party the benefit of every defensive preparation they earned.

entries.name: If the Chorus Chamber Still Functions
entries: Tyren retains a campaign-specific legendary/lair option:

entries.name: Seize the Anchored
entries: The target makes a {@dc 18} Wisdom save.
On a failure, Tyren imposes one Command-like imperative on the target’s next turn, following the campaign’s hard ceiling:

items: one compelled turn/action only;
no forced attack on an ally;
no expenditure of a major limited resource;
no irreversible roleplay decision;
no suicidal order.

entries: A {@item Ring of Mind Shielding} makes the wearer immune.
Brakkus and Bishop Brann are immune if they are somehow present.
If the Chorus Chamber was disabled, Tyren {@b cannot use this ability}.

entries.name: If the Civic Relay Still Functions
entries: Add one limited support complication rather than a full army:

items: 2 controlled {@b Veterans} arrive at the start of round 2; or
one controlled {@creature Mage|XMM} supports from a balcony until freed/defeated; or
a civic defense mechanism creates cover/hazard for Tyren.

entries: Only one of the three effects is active at a time.
If the Civic Relay was disabled, Tyren fights without controlled Bellweather support.

entries.name: If the Well Reversal Was Only Partially Stabilized
entries: Use one additional environmental effect at initiative count 20:

items: psychic shockwave causing forced movement;
radiant eruption from a marked zone;
temporary difficult terrain as gravity/force bends toward the Well.

entries: A completely stabilized Well removes this extra effect.

entries.name: Tyren’s Tactics
entries: Tyren has spent fifty years thinking about control.
He should fight intelligently.
He uses mobility, psychic abilities, breath weapon, terrain, and isolation rather than standing in melee until dead.
He recognizes the Ring of Mind Shielding as a threat if its immunity becomes obvious.
He understands Brakkus and Brann are the same kind of problem the Unturned were.
He does not waste turns repeatedly attempting effects on creatures he knows are immune.

entries.name: No Forced PvP
entries: Even in the final fight, Tyren’s anchored-mind control does not force a PC to attack another PC.
Keep the premise consistent all the way to the end.

entries.name: Tyren at 0 Hit Points
entries: The campaign established that killing a host was not automatically enough to kill Tyren.
The final objectives determine whether that remains a problem.

entries.name: If the Chorus Chamber Was Disabled
entries: Tyren’s external network has collapsed.
When his physical body dies, there is no prepared web of dominated minds for his consciousness to inhabit.
The Radiant Well pulls the remaining psychic presence inward and it dies with the dragon.
The threat ends.

entries.name: If the Chorus Chamber Still Functions
entries: Tyren attempts to escape through the remaining network.
Run a short final objective challenge: {@b 4 successes before 3 complications}.
Valid actions include:

items: destroying the Chorus system now;
using the Radiant Well to pull the escaping mind inward;
using the Ring of Mind Shielding as a protected contact point while manipulating the network;
Arcana or Religion to complete the old containment sequence;
{@i Dispel Magic}, {@i Greater Restoration}, or another relevant high-level spell used creatively;
severing controlled NPCs from the relay;
another plausible player plan.

entries: Failure should create a costly complication, not erase the campaign victory outright. Tyren may leave behind a fragment, scar, or future threat, but he does not simply possess a PC and declare the campaign lost.

entries.name: Perrin After Tyren
entries: Separating or killing Tyren does not automatically absolve Perrin.
The relevant facts remain:

items: Perrin willingly accepted supernatural influence;
he used it to manipulate people;
he organized criminals to discredit the Council;
he concealed Tyren’s independent control after discovering it;
he knowingly chose direct mental control at Storen Gate;
he continued after learning Tyren was the same force that nearly destroyed old Bellweather;
he used civic authority against the party at Zennar;
he attempted to make control permanent.

entries: Perrin was deceived about Tyren’s identity.
Perrin was also corrupted through his own choices.
Let the players and surviving Bellweather institutions decide what happens next.
Possible outcomes include trial, imprisonment, exile, political collapse, cooperation in repairing the damage, or another consequence earned through play.
Perrin’s ultimate fate is left to the players and the world; neither redemption nor execution is predetermined.

entries.name: The Radiant Well
entries: After Tyren is defeated, the Well remains.
The party and Bellweather must decide what to do with a source of power capable of both containment and mass psychic amplification.
Possible choices include:

items: seal access;
destroy the control infrastructure while preserving the natural/magical Well;
place it under shared custody among multiple institutions;
study it under strict safeguards;
collapse Varen’s lower chamber;
another player-created solution.

entries: No single Council member automatically gets control.
Brakkus’s only strong position is that no one person should quietly control something capable of taking away another person’s will.
Brann emphasizes consent and the moral danger of “good” coercion.
Ulric wants transparent legal custody and records.
Wern wants to know how the city defends the site from whoever comes next.

entries.name: Epilogue: No Cause for Alarm
entries: A public celebration belongs in the epilogue only if it matches the table’s outcome.
Show concrete consequences:

items: people waking from control and learning what they did;
businesses deciding whether Perrin-era agreements still stand;
guards confronting orders they carried out under influence;
families returning to normal routines;
political arguments happening openly again;
Ledger House full of people disagreeing loudly because they are finally allowed to.

entries: The hopeful ending is not that Bellweather becomes calm.
It is that Bellweather becomes capable of tolerating disagreement without treating disagreement as failure.
If the title gets one final spoken callback, earn it from the actual ending.
A surviving official might begin another reassuring notice and stop before writing the familiar phrase.
Brakkus might be asked whether the city is safe now and answer with something dry rather than certainty.
The final title phrase is optional and follows the actual outcome.
The campaign has already taught the table what they mean.

data.name: Appendix A: Campaign Control Sheet
entries: Use this page between sessions. It is the simplest possible version of the campaign behind the screen.

entries.name: The Truth
entries: {@b Perrin wanted enough influence to restore the Cardon fortune and make Bellweather vibrant again.}
{@b Tyren offered that power while pretending to be the Spirit of the City.}
{@b Perrin organized criminals to discredit the Council.}
{@b Tyren used the connected criminal network to experiment with mass mind control.}
{@b Perrin discovered this and kept the bargain.}
{@b Perrin eventually decided direct control worked better than influence.}
{@b Tyren is an ancient emerald dragon trapped in the Radiant Cage beneath Varen Keep.}
{@b Tyren wants complete control of every mind in the world.}
{@b Bellweather is his prototype.}

entries.name: Perrin Corruption Track
entries: Advance the track when the corresponding story choice happens, not because a certain number of sessions passed. Advance it when the corresponding story choice happens.

rows: “I can help people choose what is good for Bellweather.”
“The Council is the obstacle. I can create the crisis that proves it.”
“I did not order what the Spirit did, but exposing it would destroy everything.”
“The results are good. Maybe the old records misunderstood.”
“The Spirit can control people, but that power can still be used responsibly.”
“Not using the power when it can save lives would be irresponsible.”
“People should not be allowed to obstruct what Bellweather needs.”
“The party threatens the city because it threatens my ability to lead it.”
“A perfectly ordered Bellweather is worth the cost.”
Dreams and light influence through Perrin
Perrin can nudge individual ordinary NPCs
Tyren uses the criminal communication structure
Tyren coordinates groups and begins Mass Suggestion-style effects
Brief Command-style pressure reaches anchored PCs/Jord; stronger control reaches ordinary NPCs
Tyren can directly control ordinary people for sustained periods
Tyren attempts citywide/worldward broadcast through the Radiant Well

data.name: Appendix B: Tyren Control Quick Rules

entries.name: Ordinary NPC — Early
entries: Use {@i {@spell suggestion}} as the rules model.

items: Wisdom save.
Charmed on failure.
Instruction must be achievable.
No obviously self-destructive command.
Damage or appropriate magic can end the effect as normal for the model.

entries.name: Ordinary NPC — Group
entries: Use {@i {@spell mass suggestion}} as the rules model.
Use this when a scene requires a coordinated group, not as a casual background power.

entries.name: Ordinary NPC — Late Direct Control
entries: Use {@i {@spell dominate person}} as the rules model.
This is for late-campaign ordinary NPCs only.
Dominate Person-style control never applies to the PCs or Jord.

entries.name: PCs and Jord
entries: Use the campaign’s {@b Command ceiling}.

items: Wisdom saving throw.
One turn / one compelled action on failure.
Full control returns immediately.
No forced attacks on allies.
No forced major resource expenditure.
No irreversible roleplay choices.
No suicidal commands.

entries.name: Brakkus and Bishop Brann
entries: Direct Tyren control fails.
No save is needed when the only effect is Tyren attempting to seize their actions.
They remain vulnerable to ordinary persuasion, deception, threats, environmental danger, and unrelated magic.

entries.name: Ring of Mind Shielding
entries: A wearer is immune to Tyren’s control because the ring prevents the unwanted telepathic connection Tyren needs to establish.
This is a campaign-specific interaction with Tyren, not a blanket rewrite of the item.

data.name: Appendix C: Clue Ladder
entries: The mystery should remain solvable even when players miss individual details.

entries.name: Phase 1 — Coordination
entries: The party should learn:

items: separate gangs use the same signals;
Iron Covenant logistics connect them;
some orders appear without a recognized issuer.

entries: Sources:

items: Kellan schedules;
Koven ledgers;
captured criminals;
the coded Blackstone ledger already held by the Council.

entries.name: Phase 2 — Historical Pattern
entries: The party should learn:

items: Old Bellweather experienced the same impossible coordination;
the name Tyren appears in sealed records;
a few people called the Unturned resisted.

entries: Sources:

items: Savin diary;
command-stone report;
old civic circular.

entries.name: Phase 3 — Possession
entries: The party should learn:

items: Tyren can occupy living hosts;
destroying a host is not necessarily enough;
the Radiant Cage forced Tyren back into his own body;
resistance seems connected to certainty of self.

entries: Sources:

items: Marren Library;
Brann/Brakkus behavior;
Paden event.

entries.name: Phase 4 — Physical Truth
entries: The party should learn:

items: Tyren is an ancient emerald dragon;
Tyren is physically alive beneath Varen Keep;
the Radiant Well powers the prison;
reversing the Well would project his mind outward.

entries: Sources:

items: Maren Isle missing volume;
Rellan oral history;
Varen machinery.

entries.name: Phase 5 — Perrin
entries: The party should be able to infer:

items: Cardon-linked money helped build the criminal network;
Perrin benefited from the crises;
Tyren needs a willing conduit;
synchronized expansion originates in Bellweather;
Perrin’s rise tracks the network’s growth.

entries: No single clue should read “Perrin did it.”
The intended reveal is a confrontation with a person the party has come to know, not finding a signed villain confession in a drawer.

data.name: Appendix D: Pepper Continuity and Payoffs

entries.name: Legal Consequence
entries: Pepper’s sentence is already established and remains exactly as established even though the campaign direction changed.

items: Five mandatory Council missions total.
Kellan’s Well is Mission 1 and unpaid for Pepper.
Missions 2–5 are paid normally.
Refusal or abandonment means jail.
House arrest at Ledger House remains until completion.

entries.name: Ulric Evern — Procedure
entries: Ulric’s strength is institutional memory.
He believes power should be recorded, limited, funded, and reviewable.
Perrin increasingly sees him as a person who can always explain why the right thing cannot happen quickly.
Late campaign, Ulric is vulnerable to Tyren’s direct control. Memory gaps and inexplicable signatures can become evidence of supernatural interference.
Ulric is not secretly corrupt unless actual play makes him so.

entries.name: Wern Ursen — Security
entries: Wern responds to growing danger with stronger security.
He should sometimes be right.
He should sometimes go too far.
Use checkpoints, curfews, aggressive patrol proposals, and rigid chains of command to make him a credible political opponent and plausible suspect without making him the hidden villain.
Perrin benefits from Wern looking authoritarian.

entries.name: Bishop Brann — Limits
entries: Brann keeps asking who pays the cost of “necessary” power.
His immunity means Perrin cannot solve Brann by controlling him.
As Perrin rises, Brann becomes more dangerous politically because he remains capable of sincere dissent when other people begin falling into supernatural agreement.

entries.name: Perrin Cardon — Results
entries: Perrin should keep producing real successes.

Let Bellweather become richer, busier, safer, and more functional under some of his policies.

data.name: Appendix I: Session Prep Template for This Version
entries: This campaign is designed so the DM does not need to write an entire session from scratch every week.
For each session, prepare only the following.

entries.name: 1. What Can Change Tonight?
entries: One sentence.
Examples:

items: The party can prove Koven House is the Covenant hub.
The party can learn Tyren controlled Old Bellweather.
Perrin can cross the line into direct control.

entries.name: 2. Three Scenes
entries: {@b Arrival/choice.} Present the problem and at least two approaches.
{@b Pressure.} Combat, investigation, social conflict, hazard, or time pressure complicates the plan.
{@b Decision.} End around a choice, objective, or confrontation that changes the situation.

entries.name: 3. Essential Information
entries: Write the clues the party must be able to obtain.
Never attach a campaign-critical clue to one pass/fail roll.

entries.name: 4. Opposition
entries: For each active group, write:

items: what it wants;
what it is doing now;
what makes it retreat, surrender, bargain, or change plans.

entries.name: 5. Perrin/Tyren Movement
entries: Ask one question:
{@b Did anything happen tonight that should change Perrin’s corruption or Tyren’s reach?}
If no, there is no forced Perrin/Tyren movement that session.
Not every session needs a main-plot reveal.

entries.name: 6. Return to Ledger House
entries: Prepare:

items: one visible city change;
one familiar face;
one consequence;
one live opportunity.

entries: That is enough.

data.name: Appendix J: Campaign Constants
entries: These are fixed facts of the campaign.

items: {@b Independent world.} Not every antagonist, crime, monster, or tragedy connects to Tyren.
{@b Bishop Brann.} Brann is not secretly evil.
{@b Wern Ursen.} Wern is not secretly evil or a hidden Tyren loyalist; his hard security choices stand on their own.
{@b Played history.} The Slums and Blackstone remain what actually happened and are not retroactively Perrin plots.
{@b Anchored minds.} PCs and Jord can never be controlled beyond one single {@spell command|XPHB}-style action.
{@b Player agency.} Mind control never decides a character’s beliefs, roleplay, or irreversible choices.
{@b Iron Covenant.} The Covenant is a criminal organization Perrin helped organize; it is not a Tyren-worshiping cult.
{@b Resistance.} An anchored sense of self creates resistance. Trauma is one possible cause of that anchoring, not a magical reward for suffering.
{@b Perrin’s responsibility.} Tyren lied about being the Spirit of the City, but Perrin remains responsible for the choices he knowingly made.
{@b Finale.} Tyren is physically released and fought as an ancient emerald dragon.
{@b Level range.} The complete campaign runs from level 3 through level 16.
{@b Structure.} Named locations remain real without becoming a mandatory reclamation checklist.
